findings.title: The KTC trade/waiver crowd DB is skipped on EVERY successful KTC scrape — `content` is only bound inside the Strategy-3 fallback, so KTC_ID_TO_NAME is never built and the FAAB crowd factor is unreachable
findings.claimUnderTest: The `partial_run_tolerable:KTC_TradeDB` / `:KTC_WaiverDB` warnings are a tolerable transient on a secondary endpoint, and the KTC crowd-sourced FAAB calibration factor is live.
findings.observed: `scrape_ktc` has three extraction strategies. `content = await page.content()` is assigned ONLY inside Strategy 3, which is guarded by `if not name_map:` (line 2268). The ID-map builder at line 2477 is guarded by `if "content" in dir() and content:` — a check on whether that local was ever bound. So on every run where KTC actually works (Strategy 1 API intercept or Strategy 2 DOM, which is what produced today's 500 rows), `content` is unbound, KTC_ID_TO_NAME stays empty, line 4006's `if SITES.get("KTC") and KTC_ID_TO_NAME` is False, and both crowd endpoints are skipped with the 'no playerID->name mapping available' warning. The condition is inverted: the crowd DB can only run on the degraded path. Downstream, `ktcCrowd` is absent from the live payload, so `crowd_bid_map_from_contract` returns {} and the 'KTC crowd-sourced calibration' factor never appears — and the FAAB response does not list it as missing either (only 4 factors, warnings=[]).

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/status | python3 -c "import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['source_health']['source_failures'])"; python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('data/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json'));print('ktcCrowd' in d)"; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"addPlayerName":"Bhayshul Tuten","budgetRemaining":100}' | python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print([f['label'] for f in d['factors']], d['warnings'])"
reproduction.expected: either a KTC crowd factor in the FAAB breakdown, or an explicit missing:true entry for it
reproduction.actual: source_failures reports both KTC_TradeDB and KTC_WaiverDB 'partial' with valueCount 0 and skipReason missing_ktc_id_map; ktcCrowd not in payload -> False; FAAB factors = ['Player value baseline','Trending bump','League historical calibration','Rival contention'], warnings = []

numericProof.formula: KTC_ID_TO_NAME populated iff Strategy 3 ran iff name_map was empty after Strategies 1+2

findings.userImpact: A user on /waivers gets a FAAB bid whose crowd-calibration input is permanently absent, presented as a complete factor breakdown with no 'missing' marker — the 15%-weight rival-contention factor IS marked missing, so the omission of the crowd factor reads as 'not applicable' rather than 'never collected'. The operator meanwhile sees two permanent amber warnings that are documented as 'tolerable transients'.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding in the ingestion area covers KTC_TradeDB/KTC_WaiverDB or the crowd-FAAB path.

findings.whatWorks: The whole downstream chain is correctly built and would work the moment the map exists: build_crowd_bid_map, crowd_bid_map_from_contract, the 70/30 blend, the _ktc_crowd_applies guard and the factor emission are all present and unit-tested. The failure is confined to one variable-scope bug in the scraper.
findings.rootCause: `content` is a Strategy-3 local; the ID-map builder guards on its existence with `"content" in dir()` rather than fetching the page source unconditionally. The guard was presumably written when Strategy 3 was the only path.
findings.requiredRepair: Hoist `content = await page.content()` out of the `if not name_map:` block (or build KTC_ID_TO_NAME from the intercepted API payload, which carries playerID+playerName directly), and stop classifying an always-skipped source as a tolerable partial. Separately, have faab_recommender emit the crowd factor with missing:true when the map is empty, matching how rival contention is handled.

findings.title: Only 2 of 21 sources cast any vote on any draft pick, and all 72 slot picks are single-source: a fresh KTC pick value sits unread in canonicalSiteValues while the anchor is IDPTradeCalc alone
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Pick rows widen the anchor set to include ktcSfTep so the two real pick markets (KTC + IDPTC) average as peers.' And the dlfRookieSf registry entry: 'The pick nudge is wired via synthetic "2026 Pick R.SS" rows that the conversion step appends to the CSV so the source's Hill value flows into pick rankDerivedValue directly.'
findings.observed: Counting non-null sourceRanks over the 144 pick rows on the live board: ktcSfTep votes on 36 (the generic Early/Mid/Late 1st-4th tiers, the only picks in ktcSfTep.csv), idpTradeCalc on 96. No other source votes on any pick. All 72 slot picks (2026 Pick 1.01 .. 6.12) have sourceCount == 1 and anchorValue == the IDPTradeCalc value, even though canonicalSiteValues carries a KTC value for every one of them (pickAnchors['ktc'] has 126 entries, interpolated by the scraper) — `ktc` was demoted to a non-voting display key in 2026-04-28 and nothing re-routed the pick anchors to ktcSfTep. Separately, all 55 dlfRookieSf synthetic pick stamps land in canonicalSiteValues (as raw synthetic rank encodings like 999880) but appear in sourceRanks on zero pick rows.

A user trading a 1.01 sees 7799 where a two-market peer average of the numbers the system already holds would be materially lower (KTC prices it 16% below IDPTC). The docs assert the opposite of what runs.

priorFinding.note: F02 concerns the pick-YEAR discount double-counting, a different stage. Nothing prior covers pick source coverage or the ktc/ktcSfTep pick-anchor split.

findings.rootCause: KTC's slot-pick values reach the contract only through `pickAnchors['ktc']`, which is stamped under the demoted non-voting `ktc` key. ktcSfTep.csv contains only the 36 generic tiers KTC publishes, so the promoted key has nothing to vote with on slot picks. The 2026-04-28 demotion of `ktc` moved the blend vote but not the pick anchors.
findings.requiredRepair: Stamp pickAnchors under `ktcSfTep` as well as `ktc` (KTC's pick board carries no TE dimension, so the two are identical for picks — they already are on all 36 shared rows), or make the pick anchor set read `ktc` explicitly. Then either wire the dlfRookieSf synthetic pick stamps into sourceRanks or stop writing them into canonicalSiteValues and correct the registry comment.
findings.dependencies: Coordinate with the value-pipeline workstream: pick tethering (Phase 5.2b) overwrites current-year slot picks, so measure the effect on 2027/2028 slots separately.

findings.title: The raw-ingest scaffold (/api/scaffold/raw, /status, /identity) serves a 2026-04-20 artifact stamped with a 2026-08-03 mtime, and no code in the tree can produce a new one

No staleness field, no warning: `warnings` is []. The snapshot covers 9 sources, two of which (FANTASYPROS_SF, FLOCK_FANTASY_SF) recorded record_count 0 at capture time with warnings still []. It also carries FOOTBALLGUYS_SF (563) + FOOTBALLGUYS_IDP (525) — 1,088 records from a vendor that is not in _RANKING_SOURCES at all and whose freshness stamp is frozen at 2026-05-24. Grepping the tree for a writer of data/raw_sources/raw_source_snapshot_*.json finds only consumers (server.py, scripts/validate_ingest.py, scripts/identity_resolve.py) and a retention pruner; no producer exists, and no workflow references the scaffold.

findings.rootCause: The scaffold's producer was removed (or never migrated out of the one-off CI run that wrote these files with /home/runner/work/... paths baked in); the read side was left registered.
findings.requiredRepair: Decide: either restore a producer wired into scheduled-refresh.yml, or remove the three routes and validate_ingest.py/identity_resolve.py's dependence on them. findings.title: The per-source deploy gate documents itself as running every 6h in health-check.yml; it does not — the 6h workflow uses a floor of 8 covered sources out of 21
findings.claimUnderTest: verify_live_source_coverage.py: 'Used at two layers so a degraded board cannot persist silently: deploy/verify-deploy.sh ... and .github/workflows/health-check.yml — every 6h against the public URL, catching drift that happens outside a deploy.'
findings.observed: `grep -rn verify_live_source_coverage .github/workflows/ deploy/` returns exactly one hit: deploy/verify-deploy.sh:340. health-check.yml instead inlines a dependency-free check with MIN_SOURCES = 8 and MIN_PER_SOURCE = 5 ('Dependency-free so this lean workflow needs no checkout'), which is designed only to separate the healthy ~16-21-source board from the catastrophic 3-source legacy export. Losing any 1 to 13 individual sources between deploys passes that gate. The strict script itself works: run against the live server it prints 'ok: live board carries 21 registered source(s); 0 fresh-but-absent'.

reproduction.expected: the strict fresh-but-absent gate running every 6h against prod
reproduction.actual: one reference only (deploy/verify-deploy.sh:340); health-check.yml uses MIN_SOURCES=8; strict script run manually returns 'ok: live board carries 21 registered source(s); 0 fresh-but-absent (0 skipped: stale/empty)'

numericProof.formula: alert iff count(sources with >=5 covered players) < 8

findings.userImpact: Between deploys (which can be days apart) the board can lose up to 13 of 21 sources without any production alert. The 2h CI watchdog (watchdog_contract_coverage.py) does cover this against the CI checkout, so the exposure is specifically 'the running prod process serves a different board than CI builds'.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers the docstring-vs-wiring mismatch for verify_live_source_coverage.py.

findings.whatWorks: Both CI watchdogs pass against the live tree right now: `watchdog_freshness.py` -> 'ok: 22 sources fresh, 0 hard-stale'; `watchdog_contract_coverage.py` -> 'ok: 21 registered source(s) covered, 0 fresh-but-absent'. The deploy-time gate is genuinely wired and would fail a deploy that served a degraded board.
findings.rootCause: The health-check workflow was deliberately kept checkout-free, so the strict script could not be invoked there; the script's docstring was written for the intended design and never corrected.
findings.requiredRepair: Either add a checkout step (or ship the per-source expectations as data in the /api/status payload so a dependency-free checker can be strict), or correct the docstring and lower MIN_SOURCES tolerance to name the expected registry count.

findings.title: Per-source staleness is computed in every /api/data payload and shown to nobody: two disagreeing threshold tables (6h in code, 24h in config) and no user-visible surface for either
findings.claimUnderTest: config/source_staleness.json's own comment: a stale source is 'reported everywhere (on-site stale banner, email alerts ..., the freshness-watchdog summary)'.
findings.observed: There is no on-site per-source stale banner. `dataFreshness.sourceTimestamps` — 22 entries each carrying ageHours, maxAgeHours and staleness fresh|stale|missing — is shipped in every /api/data response and is read by exactly one module in the tree, `src/consensus_edge/service.py`, whose feature flag is OFF by default (ADR-023). The frontend touches `dataFreshness` in one place, rankings/page.jsx:835, and reads only `generatedAt` for a whole-board 'updated Xm ago'. StaleDataBanner polls /api/health and shows a single whole-board `data_age_hours`. Two independent threshold tables disagree by 4x: `_SOURCE_MAX_AGE_HOURS` in data_contract.py sets 6h for ktc/ktcSfTep/idpTradeCalc/dynastyNerdsSfTep/fantasyProsIdp/dynastyDaddySf/fantasyCalc/otcffbSf/draftSharks/draftSharksIdp/fantasyNavigatorSf/pfkDynasty; config/source_staleness.json sets 24h for every source. The 6h table is the one that stamps the payload; the 24h table is the one that fires email. Neither reaches a user. Finally, staleness is purely descriptive: nothing downweights or drops a stale source's vote.

findings.userImpact: A single dead source (the documented idpShow-cookie-lapse mode) is invisible on-site: the whole-board age stays fresh because 20 other sources refresh, /tools/source-health does not list the source at all (W05-F001), and only an email alert fires — and only if ALERT_TO is configured. priorFinding.note: F13 ('staleness is reporting-only; a stale source votes at full weight') reproduced: nothing in _compute_unified_rankings reads sourceTimestamps.staleness. Also PRIOR-A25-F04 ('the contract calls 12 sources stale while the watchdog calls all 22 fresh') is NOT reproducible at HEAD — every source reads fresh under both tables today (all ageHours 1.66-1.86 vs thresholds of 6 and 24), because _build_source_timestamps now prefers the data/scrape_state stamp over CSV mtime. findings.whatWorks: The email alert path is real and correctly per-source: _build_source_health_snapshot's `sources` block (22 correct entries) feeds src/api/source_health_alerts.check_and_alert from the daily /api/signal-alerts/run sweep, with a documented soft/soft-escalate policy for idpShow. findings.requiredRepair: Collapse to one threshold source of truth (config/source_staleness.json, via resolve_threshold) and have _build_source_timestamps call it. Then render sourceTimestamps on /tools/source-health as part of the W05-F001 fix.

findings.title: The GitHub-Actions 2h refresh cron misses roughly a quarter of its cycles while the prod systemd fetch timers hit every one
findings.claimUnderTest: 'Runs the scraper + canonical rebuild every 2 hours' (cron '42 */2 * * *').
findings.observed: Reading the commit stream the workflow itself produces ('chore: freshness stamps <UTC>'), over the 26.7h window 2026-08-03T15:37Z to 2026-08-04T18:21Z there are 10 runs where 13-14 are scheduled. Inter-run gaps: 2.87, 1.85, 1.53, 2.08, 4.00, 3.50, 3.75, 4.00, 3.13 hours — three gaps at or above 3.5h and one full missed cycle. Over the same window the prod-side systemd fetch timers land exactly on cadence (dlf at :27 and idpShow at :32 of every even UTC hour, 14/14 runs, zero misses).

reproduction.command: git log --since='2026-08-02' --format='%s' -- data/scrape_state | grep 'freshness stamps' | head -20
reproduction.expected: ~13 runs in 26.7h at a 2h cadence

numericProof.formula: missed_fraction = 1 - observed/expected

findings.userImpact: Board data is up to 4h old rather than 2h at the worst points. Not a correctness defect, but it interacts with W05-F009: the 6h maxAgeHours budgets in _SOURCE_MAX_AGE_HOURS assume a 2h cadence ('6 hours ≈ three missed cycles'); at the observed cadence a 6h budget is closer to 1.5 missed cycles of headroom.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced with a different window and method (workflow-authored commit timestamps rather than run history). My measurement is 10/13 (~23% missed) over 26.7h. Confidence is medium rather than high because the commit stream is a proxy for the run stream — a run that produced no stamp change would not appear — though the workflow force-adds data/scrape_state/ every run, so that should be rare.

findings.whatWorks: The prod-side systemd fetch timers (dlf, idpShow) are perfectly regular over the same window, so this is specific to GitHub Actions' documented best-effort cron.
findings.rootCause: GitHub Actions schedule events are best-effort and are dropped under load; nothing compensates.
findings.requiredRepair: Either accept and document the real cadence (and widen the freshness budgets that assume 2h), or move the scrape trigger to the prod host's systemd timers, which are demonstrably reliable here, with Actions as a backstop.

findings.title: Two real players occupy two board rows each because name-variant drift splits one human across a resolved row and an unresolved ghost, stranding vendor votes
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md and src/identity/matcher.py:17-30 claim the position-aware canonical key prevents two rows for one player; validationSummary.duplicateCanonicalIdentityCount is the pinned detector.
findings.observed: The live 1,092-row contract carries BOTH 'Matt Hibner' (playerId 13324, TE/BAL/24, rank 377, rankDerivedValue 1737, sourceCount 8) and 'Matthew Hibner' (playerId null, position null, same team BAL, same age 24) - the same human. The three source CSVs (ktc, ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc) spell him 'Matthew Hibner', so their values 891/1458/1129 are stamped byte-identically on BOTH rows. dlfSf (rank 250.83), flockFantasySf (383.0) and draftSharks (400.0) land ONLY on the ghost, so the priced row blends 8 of 11 available vendor votes. Second case: 'Jam Miller' (playerId 13403, RB/NE, rank 635) vs 'Jamarion Miller' (playerId null) - DraftSharks' own CSV analysis text for 'Jamarion Miller' reads "Miller could make the Patriots roster as a third RB", identifying the same player; its rank-323 vote is stranded on the ghost. buildRows materializes both: /rankings renders 'Matt Hibner' at rank 377 AND 'Matthew Hibner' at rank 1052. validationSummary.duplicateCanonicalIdentityCount = 0 because that detector keys on exact _normalize_for_collision equality, and the split exists precisely because the keys differ.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/repro_duplicates.py
reproduction.expected: 0 split identities; every human occupies exactly one board row
reproduction.actual: 1 CONFIRMED (Matthew/Matt Hibner, team+age identical, 3 byte-identical source values) + 1 REVIEW (Jamarion/Jam Miller); contract reports duplicateCanonicalIdentityCount=0

numericProof.formula: blendedSourceRank = (mean(ranks) + median(ranks)) / 2  [count-aware mean-median, n>=5 branch]

findings.userImpact: A user searching /rankings for 'Hibner' sees the player twice - once at #377 with a value and once at #1052 without - and cannot tell which is real. The priced row's value is computed from 73% of the vendor votes the pipeline actually loaded for that player, so its rank is wrong by an unknown amount in the trade calculator, the finder and every engine that reads rankDerivedValue.

priorFinding.note: A24-F05 measured 0 name COLLISIONS in the pool builder and called the path inert. The live failure is the inverse class - a SPLIT, not a merge - which no prior finding names and which A24-F05's collision measurement structurally cannot see.

findings.whatWorks: 0 duplicate playerIds and 0 duplicate position-aware canonical keys across all 1,092 rows; the position-aware key does prevent the Quay-Walker/Kenneth-Walker merge class it was built for.
findings.rootCause: The merge key is a canonical NAME (Dynasty Scraper.py:4655 `entry = players_json.get(canonical, ...)`), and CANONICAL_NAME_ALIASES has entries for Kenneth->Kenny and Chig->Chigoziem but none for Matt<->Matthew or Jam<->Jamarion. The scraper's must_have_rookie_guarantee fallback then mints a second row for the unaliased spelling, and _enrich_from_source_csvs grafts CSV values onto whichever row matches each vendor's spelling.
findings.requiredRepair: Deduplicate playersArray on sleeperId after enrichment, and add a near-name split detector (same surname + similarity >= 0.85 + exactly one side has no playerId) that raises a real flag instead of the hardcoded nearNameMismatchCount: 0. Alias-table additions treat symptoms, not the class.

findings.title: Both identity-duplicate detectors on the contract are structurally unable to fire, and scripts/audit_identity.py renders a permanently empty section for the one that would have caught W06-F001
findings.claimUnderTest: _validate_and_quarantine_rows docstring: 'Check 0: position-aware duplicate identity ... This is the entity-resolution duplicate the build-time assertion test will also surface.' scripts/audit_identity.py advertises 'Near-name value mismatches (same last name, different universes)' as report #6.
findings.observed: Check 0 indexes on f"{_normalize_for_collision(name)}::{group}" - exact-key equality. A split identity has, by definition, two different keys, so the detector can never see it. The near-name rule that WOULD have seen it was retired: near_name_pairs is permanently [] and "nearNameMismatchCount": 0 is a literal at data_contract.py:3330. scripts/audit_identity.py reads validation['nearNameMismatches'] and prints '(none)'. Live output: NEAR-NAME VALUE MISMATCHES '(none)', CROSS-UNIVERSE NAME COLLISIONS '(none)', quarantined=1 (Brandon Knight, unsupported_position). An operator running the repo's own identity audit gets a clean bill on a board that demonstrably carries a split player.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python scripts/audit_identity.py --json-path docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json
reproduction.expected: the near-name section reports Matt/Matthew Hibner and Jam/Jamarion Miller
reproduction.actual: 'NEAR-NAME VALUE MISMATCHES ... (none)' and 'CROSS-UNIVERSE NAME COLLISIONS ... (none)'

numericProof.formula: detector_hits = |{rows sharing an exact position-aware collision key}| + nearNameMismatchCount

findings.userImpact: Nobody is told the board contains a duplicated player, so the wrong value in W06-F001 ships with a 'validated' stamp.

priorFinding.note: A12-F18 established nearNameMismatchCount is hardcoded 0 and the dead threshold constant. Confirmed, and extended: the retirement is what makes W06-F001 invisible, and scripts/audit_identity.py still advertises the retired check as report #6.

findings.whatWorks: The quarantine pass itself runs on every build and does flag unsupported_position (Brandon Knight, T) and suspicious_disagreement (50 rows) with correct confidence degradation.
findings.rootCause: The only surviving duplicate detector is exact-key; the fuzzy one was removed for false positives and replaced with a literal 0 rather than a tighter rule.
findings.requiredRepair: Re-introduce a near-name detector scoped to (same surname AND >=0.85 similarity AND exactly one side lacks playerId) - that predicate produces 1 confirmed hit and 0 false positives on today's board, versus the 40+ the retired rule produced.

findings.title: /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized returns unmapped_player for every player because the Sleeper block never contains the key the identity mapper is handed
findings.claimUnderTest: server.py:11260 'Find this player's GSIS via the unified mapper, then filter.' The route's own comment says the row-filter bug was the defect and was fixed.
findings.observed: players_dir = sleeper_block.get("players") or sleeper_block.get("playerDict"). The Sleeper block the scraper writes (Dynasty Scraper.py:1297-1306) contains exactly leagueId, leagueName, teams, positions, playerIds, idToPlayer, scoringSettings, rosterPositions, leagueSettings - no 'players', no 'playerDict', ever. players_dir is therefore always None, _index_directory(None) returns four empty dicts, resolve_player returns None, and the route short-circuits at reason: unmapped_player. Confirmed live on four real Sleeper ids (A.J. Brown 5859, Josh Allen 4984, Bijan Robinson 9509, Kenny Gainwell 7567): all four return unmapped_player. The stats fetch SUCCEEDS first (the route would otherwise say no_stats_available), so the mapper is the sole blocker. /api/status corroborates: idMappingCoverage = {resolve_attempts: 8, unresolved: 8, coverage_pct: 0.0}. This is a key-name mismatch in committed code, not container state.

reproduction.command: for sid in 5859 4984 9509 7567; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/player/$sid/realized"; echo; done
reproduction.expected: weekly realized-points arrays for each player
reproduction.actual: {"sleeperId":"5859","leagueKey":"dynasty_main","reason":"unmapped_player","weeks":[]} for all four

numericProof.formula: resolvable = |{sid : sleeper_block['players'] is a dict and sid in it}|

findings.userImpact: PlayerPopup's realized-points panel is empty for every player in every league. A user comparing a player's market value against his actual production sees nothing and concludes there is no data.

priorFinding.note: A22-F03 claims the route 'emits a full array of 0.0-point weeks'; A22-F02 claims IDP players 'silently return zero weeks'. Neither reproduces: the route never reaches the scoring stage for ANY player. Both describe behaviour downstream of a bail that always fires. Same for PRIOR-A21-F16's league-scoping claim - the response never contains weeks to mis-score.

findings.whatWorks: The route's auth gate, flag gate, league resolution and the nfl_data weekly fetch all work - the fetch returns rows, which is why the response is unmapped_player rather than no_stats_available.
findings.rootCause: server.py reads sleeper.players / sleeper.playerDict; the producer emits sleeper.playerIds (name->id) and sleeper.idToPlayer (id->name). No writer has ever produced the key the reader asks for.
findings.requiredRepair: Either fetch the Sleeper player directory for the mapper, or resolve the GSIS id from idToPlayer[sid] plus the nflverse name index. A key rename alone is NOT enough - playerIds/idToPlayer carry no gsis_id.

findings.title: config/identity/id_overrides.json cannot influence the board at all, and where it IS read the override loses to the directory it exists to override
findings.claimUnderTest: unified_mapper docstring: 'UDFAs, practice-squad callups, and same-name-different-player cases live in config/identity/id_overrides.json - a flat map that short-circuits the match ladder.'
findings.observed: Two separate failures. (1) SCOPE: neither Dynasty Scraper.py nor src/api/data_contract.py reads the file. Its only readers are unified_mapper.resolve_player (reachable solely from the always-failing /api/player/{id}/realized, see W06-F003) and src/playerctx/normalize.py. No override can affect a single value on the board. (2) PRECEDENCE: the override rung is step 2, AFTER the exact-sleeper_id rung at :275. Proven at runtime: with a directory containing sleeper_id 999 and an override for 999, resolve_player returns the DIRECTORY row (match_method='sleeper_id'); the override only fires when the directory has no such id. Since the documented use cases ('same-name-different-player', 'players with identical names across positions') are by definition players the Sleeper directory already knows, the override layer is unreachable for its stated purpose. src/playerctx/normalize.py:561-563 independently documents this from the other side. (3) The shipped file contains only _comment and _example_entry_only, and _example_entry_only is loaded as a live override key.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/repro_overrides_and_mapper.py
reproduction.expected: section B prints 'manual_override / OVERRIDE NAME / 00-9999999'
reproduction.actual: section B prints 'sleeper_id / DIRECTORY NAME / gsis 00-0000001'; live override keys = ['_example_entry_only']

numericProof.formula: board_rows_influenced_by_overrides = |{row : row.playerId set via an override}|

findings.userImpact: An operator who edits id_overrides.json to fix a mis-identified player, redeploys, and re-scrapes sees no change on any board and gets no error - the documented remediation path for identity defects is inert.

priorFinding.note: A24-F04's secondary note observes the empty-map cache re-read. The precedence inversion (override loses to the directory) and the total absence of the file from the board path are new, and are proven at runtime here rather than by reading.

findings.whatWorks: _load_overrides degrades correctly on a missing or malformed file (logs and returns {}), and reload_overrides behaves as documented.
findings.rootCause: Ladder ordering: exact sleeper_id (step 1) is checked before the manual override (step 2), and no board-building module imports the loader at all.
findings.requiredRepair: Move the override rung above the exact-id rung, and give the board path a real consumer - the natural one is Dynasty Scraper.py::_resolve_sleeper_identity, where every board playerId is actually assigned.

findings.title: identityConfidence is a three-valued restatement of 'does this row have a playerId', that playerId was itself assigned by a name match, and no surface reads the field
findings.claimUnderTest: _compute_identity_confidence documents a four-rung ladder (1.00 canonical_id / 0.95 position_source_aligned / 0.85 partial_evidence / 0.70 name_only) scoring 'how confident we are that this row represents the right entity'.
findings.observed: Live distribution over 1,092 rows: 1.00 canonical_id x937, 0.95 position_source_aligned x144 (every pick, via the assetClass=='pick' short-circuit), 0.70 name_only x11. The 0.85 partial_evidence rung emits zero rows. The field is therefore a bijection with (playerId is not None, assetClass=='pick') - it adds no information. Worse, the 1.00 label is not earned: no source except pfkDynasty publishes a Sleeper id, and every playerId on the board comes from Dynasty Scraper.py::_resolve_sleeper_identity, a NAME lookup with a 0.90-threshold difflib fallback. Consumption: buildRows copies identityConfidence/identityMethod onto every row (dynasty-data.js:1151-1152, 1295-1296, 1782-1783), and a repo-wide grep across frontend/app, frontend/components and frontend/lib finds ZERO non-test readers. Only the sibling `quarantined` boolean is read (/rankings trust tile, /edge filters). Corroborating: the one quarantined row on today's board, Brandon Knight, is stamped identityConfidence 1.00.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,collections; d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json')); print(collections.Counter((r['identityConfidence'], r['identityMethod']) for r in d['playersArray']))"
reproduction.expected: a spread across four rungs reflecting match quality
reproduction.actual: Counter({(1.0,'canonical_id'):937, (0.95,'position_source_aligned'):144, (0.7,'name_only'):11})

numericProof.formula: identityConfidence == 1.00 iff playerId != null; == 0.95 iff assetClass=='pick'; else 0.70

findings.userImpact: No direct user-facing number, but every downstream reader that treats 'identityConfidence 1.00' as evidence of a correct match is trusting a name join - including the Hibner row in W06-F001, which is stamped 1.00.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced A24-F02 and A12-F17 (identical 937/144/11 split, dead 0.85 rung). Extended in two ways they do not cover: the field has zero non-test consumers anywhere in the frontend, and the one row the quarantine pass flags is itself stamped 1.00.

findings.whatWorks: identityMethod is internally consistent with identityConfidence, and the 11 name_only rows are genuinely the 11 rows with no Sleeper id.
findings.rootCause: The score is computed from field presence rather than from the join that actually happened; the join method is never recorded on the row.
findings.requiredRepair: Stamp the real join provenance from the enrichment cascade (sleeper_id / exact canonical name / alias-table / fuzzy) instead of re-deriving a score from playerId presence, then either render it or delete it.

findings.title: unified_mapper.resolve_player merges 11 demonstrably different NFL players at its default threshold on today's real corpus, and the scraper's own fuzzy guard passes 5 of the same 11 pairs
findings.claimUnderTest: Module docstring: 'Fuzzy normalized name only. confidence=0.75..0.90 ... Anything below the configured min_confidence is rejected.' _is_safe_name_merge: 'Guard fuzzy canonicalization so unrelated players are not merged.'
findings.observed: Fed the 544 distinct source-CSV names that FAILED the production canonical-name join, plus a directory built from the live 948-player board, resolve_player(min_confidence=0.85) returns a match for 11 of them - every one a different human, each reported at confidence 0.857-0.923 with match_method='fuzzy_name' (a method the docstring caps at 0.90): Tevin Coleman->Kevin Coleman 0.923, Ian Thomas->Brian Thomas 0.909, Eric Gray->Cedric Gray 0.900, Ty Montgomery->Tyren Montgomery 0.897, Mike Williams->Mykel Williams 0.889, Cedrick Wilson->Eric Wilson 0.880, Jordan Travis->Jordan Davis 0.880, Jacob Harris->Jacob Parrish 0.880, Amari Cooper->Omar Cooper 0.870, Jordan Wilkins->Jordan Watkins 0.857. Separately, the ladder has no name+team rung: with two 'Josh Allen' rows (QB/BUF and LB/JAX) and no position supplied, resolve_player(name='Josh Allen', team='JAX') returns the BUF QB at confidence 1.00 - the caller's team is ignored entirely and the answer flips with dict insertion order. Blast radius is bounded by reachability: the live board join uses exact _canonical_match_key and correctly rejected all 544. But the scraper's OWN guard, _is_safe_name_merge, returns True for 5 of the 11 pairs (Tevin/Kevin Coleman, Ian/Brian Thomas, Eric/Cedric Gray, Cedrick Wilson/Eric Wilson, Cedrick Wilson Jr./Eric Wilson), and best_match is called at threshold 0.85 (line 4473) and 0.90 (4586, 5339) - so three of those pairs clear both the guard and the 0.90 gate on the live scrape path.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/repro_overrides_and_mapper.py  # sections C+D; full 11-pair sweep captured in fuzzy-false-merges.json
reproduction.expected: 0 matches among CSV names the exact join already rejected
reproduction.actual: 11 matches, confidence 0.857-0.923, all cross-player; and name+team resolution ignores team

numericProof.formula: false_merges = |{n : resolve_player(board_directory, name=n, min_confidence=0.85) is not None}| over names the exact canonical join rejected

findings.userImpact: Not a live wrong number on the board today (the board join is exact). It is a loaded gun: any future caller that routes a source through resolve_player, and the scraper's own 0.85/0.90 fuzzy rungs, will attribute one player's value to another and report it above 0.85 confidence.

priorFinding.note: A24-F03 demonstrated the threshold problem on hand-picked name pairs. Confirmed and extended: measured against the 544 names the LIVE corpus actually fails to join (11 false merges), plus the new finding that Dynasty Scraper.py's _is_safe_name_merge guard admits 5 of those same pairs, so the defect is not confined to the unreachable module.

findings.whatWorks: The exact-key production join (_canonical_match_key) rejected all 544 unmatched names with zero false merges - the conservative path is the one actually in use on the board.
findings.rootCause: min_confidence is compared against a raw difflib ratio with no length, token or edit-position weighting; the fuzzy result overwrites confidence with that ratio; and there is no name+team rung between name+team+pos and name+pos.
findings.requiredRepair: Require a surname exact match plus a first-name compatibility check before any fuzzy accept (the pool builder's _first_name_compatible already exists), add a name+team rung, and never report a fuzzy match above 0.90.

findings.title: resolve_many rebuilds the entire Sleeper directory index once per input row - 203x its own documented cost
findings.claimUnderTest: resolve_many docstring: 'Used by nightly jobs (injury feed, nflverse weekly ingest) so the mapper's internal index is built once, not per-row.'
findings.observed: _index_directory sits inside resolve_player (:269), and resolve_many loops resolve_player. Measured on an 11,000-entry directory (Sleeper's real order of magnitude) with 200 inputs: 14.592s total vs 0.072s for a single index build - 199 redundant rebuilds, 99.5% of wall time. src/playerctx/normalize.py:551 documents the same problem and builds its own indexes to avoid it.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/repro_overrides_and_mapper.py  # section D
reproduction.expected: ~0.08s (one index build) for 200 rows

numericProof.formula: t_actual / t_one_index_build

findings.userImpact: No user-facing effect today (the batch path has no live caller), but any nightly job wired to it would take minutes instead of seconds.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed by direct timing rather than by reading; A24-F04 asserted the structure, this measures the 203x.

findings.whatWorks: resolve_many's contract (returning unresolved rows verbatim) is honoured.
findings.rootCause: Index construction is inside the per-row function.
findings.requiredRepair: Hoist _index_directory into resolve_many and pass the prebuilt index down; keep resolve_player's single-row convenience wrapper.

findings.title: Draft picks have no structured identity on the live path: season, round and slot exist only as substrings of a display name, re-parsed by at least nine divergent regexes, and the PickRow model that declares them is dead code
findings.claimUnderTest: src/identity/models.py::PickRow declares season, round, slot_known, slot_number, bucket, league_id - the canonical pick identity. matcher.py branches on rec.asset_type == 'pick' to populate it.
findings.observed: On the live contract's 144 pick rows, NONE of season / year / round / slot / originalOwner / currentOwner / projectedSlot exists as a field. playerId is null on all 144. The only identity is the displayName string ('2026 Pick 1.02', '2027 Early 1st'). Original and current owner do not exist in the contract at all - ownership lives only in sleeper.teams[].pickDetails and the draft-capital fallback. PickRow is unreachable on real data: src/adapters/scraper_bridge_adapter.py:101 hardcodes asset_type='player', so all 3,494 records in the newest raw snapshot are typed 'player' and matcher.py's pick branch never executes - /api/scaffold/identity reports pick_count 0 / pick_alias_count 0 while minting 84 master PLAYERS with ids like 'player::2026 early 1st::OTHER'. In place of the model, at least nine modules re-derive season/round/slot from the name with their own regexes, and they disagree: frontend/lib/pick-stack.js TIER_RE accepts rounds 1-9, data_contract._PICK_TIER_RE accepts 1-6; canonical/normalization_validator requires a two-digit slot (\.\d{2}) while _PICK_SLOT_RE accepts (0?[1-9]|1[0-2]); pool/builder caps the slot at 12.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json')); p=[r for r in d['playersArray'] if r['assetClass']=='pick']; print(len(p)); print({k:sum(1 for x in p if x.get(k) is not None) for k in ['season','round','slot','originalOwner','currentOwner','projectedSlot','playerId']})" && curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/scaffold/identity | head -c 220
reproduction.expected: season/round/slot populated on all 144 picks; scaffold pick_count == 144
reproduction.actual: {'season':0,'round':0,'slot':0,'originalOwner':0,'currentOwner':0,'projectedSlot':0,'playerId':0}; scaffold reports pick_count 0, pick_alias_count 0

numericProof.formula: structured_pick_identity_coverage = fields_present / (144 rows x 5 canonical fields)

findings.userImpact: Every surface that needs a pick's year, round or slot re-parses a display string, so a label the scraper emits in an unexpected shape (a 14-team slot, a one-digit slot, a round above 6) is silently classified as a PLAYER by some modules and a pick by others - the same asset then gets a player's treatment on one page and a pick's on another, with no error.

priorFinding.note: A24-F28 found one symptom (pool/builder's slot regex caps at 12). No prior finding states the underlying condition: there is no structured pick identity on the live path at all, and the model that declares one is unreachable because every raw record is typed 'player'.

findings.whatWorks: pickAliases is internally consistent: all 18 generic->slot aliases (Early->x.02, Mid->x.06, Late->x.10) resolve to a slot row that carries a real rankDerivedValue, and every aliased generic row is correctly suppressed (rankDerivedValue null, pickGenericSuppressed true), so no double-count is possible on the 2026 class.
findings.rootCause: The adapter that feeds the identity layer hardcodes asset_type='player', and the contract layer never promoted the parsed (year, round, slot) tuple from _PICK_SLOT_RE into row fields.
findings.requiredRepair: Stamp season/round/slot (and slotKnown) onto every pick row in the contract once, from the parse the contract already performs, and have every consumer read those fields instead of re-parsing the name. Fixing asset_type in the bridge adapter is a prerequisite for the scaffold layer.

findings.title: dynastyNerdsSfTep.csv ships a stable SleeperId column that the ID-join alias list cannot see, so a 294-row source joins by name only
findings.claimUnderTest: data_contract.py:3570-3574: 'Optional Sleeper player-id column (today only pfkDynasty emits one). When present it gives ID-grade identity that survives vendor/Sleeper name-spelling drift.'
findings.observed: dynastyNerdsSfTep.csv's header is Name,Rank,Value,SleeperId,Pos,Team - it emits one. _SLEEPER_ID_ALIASES = ('sleeper_id','sleeperId','sleeper_player_id') and _pick does an exact, case-sensitive dict lookup, so 'SleeperId' never matches. Measured: the parsed lookup for dynastyNerdsSfTep carries a sleeperId on 0 of 294 rows, versus 496 of 496 for pfkDynasty. Rescue value TODAY is zero (only 1 DynastyNerds row fails the name join - Dare Ogunbowale, who has no board row either), so this is latent, not live. The same measurement shows pfkDynasty's working ID join also rescues 0 rows today: 20 name misses, none corresponding to a board row. In other words, 100% of source->board joins on the live board are name joins.

reproduction.expected: dynastyNerdsSfTep 294 with sleeperId: 294
reproduction.actual: dynastyNerdsSfTep 294 with sleeperId: 0 | pfkDynasty 496 with sleeperId: 496

numericProof.formula: parsed_ids = |{row : _pick(row, _SLEEPER_ID_ALIASES) != ''}|

findings.userImpact: None today. Becomes real the moment DynastyNerds and Sleeper disagree on a spelling - that vendor's vote is then dropped from the blend with no warning, exactly the failure the pfkDynasty ID join was added to prevent.

priorFinding.note: Confirms docs/identity-audit-2026-07.md recommendation #1 as re-stated by A24-F26, and adds the measurement that neither ID join (Nerds or PFK) rescues a single row on the live board - every source->board join today is a name join.

findings.whatWorks: pfkDynasty's sleeper_id column parses on 496/496 rows and the sid_index/audit-alias plumbing behaves as documented.
findings.rootCause: Case-sensitive exact key lookup against a fixed alias tuple.
findings.requiredRepair: Case-fold the header keys once when building each csvrow, or add 'SleeperId' to _SLEEPER_ID_ALIASES.

findings.title: /api/scaffold/identity serves a 106-day-old identity report whose master players carry zero Sleeper IDs and whose pick table is empty, with no staleness marker on the response
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md lists GET /api/scaffold/identity as a live endpoint serving 'Identity mappings'.
findings.observed: The endpoint returns 2.5 MB with generated_at 2026-04-20T19:48:28Z - 106 days before the live contract's 2026-08-04 - and the payload carries no age field. Contents: master_player_count 1788, player_alias_count 3494, pick_count 0, pick_alias_count 0, low_confidence_count 1906 (54.5% of aliases, ALL method 'exact_name_only'), and sleeper_id populated on 0 of 1788 master players because matcher.py:132 hardcodes sleeper_id="". 84 of the 1788 masters are draft picks minted as 'player::2026 early 1st::OTHER'. The producer scripts/identity_resolve.py is referenced by no workflow, timer or service, writes files named identity_resolution_*.json (zero exist on disk), and reads a raw snapshot whose newest file is also 2026-04-20. So the surface is a name-keyed master with no IDs, no picks, and no producer, served as current.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/scaffold/identity | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print({k:v for k,v in d.items() if not isinstance(v,list)}); print('sleeper_id populated:', sum(1 for p in d['players'] if p.get('sleeper_id')), 'of', len(d['players']))"
reproduction.expected: a report generated alongside the current contract, with sleeper_id populated and pick_count 144
reproduction.actual: generated_at 2026-04-20, pick_count 0, sleeper_id populated: 0 of 1788, low_confidence_count 1906

numericProof.formula: staleness_days = contract_date - report_date ; id_coverage = masters_with_sleeper_id / masters

findings.userImpact: Any operator or integration reading /api/scaffold/identity to answer 'which player is this' gets a four-month-old, ID-free, pick-free answer presented as current.

priorFinding.note: Confirms A25-F10 / A23-F15 / A24-F23 on staleness and the missing producer. Extended with two measurements none of them make: sleeper_id is populated on 0 of 1788 masters (hardcoded empty at matcher.py:132) and pick_count is 0 because every raw record is typed 'player', so the whole PickRow branch is dead.

findings.whatWorks: /api/scaffold/status DOES expose the file mtime, so the staleness is discoverable one endpoint away.
findings.rootCause: matcher.py never resolves a Sleeper id, the bridge adapter never emits asset_type='pick', and no scheduler runs the producer.
findings.requiredRepair: Either retire the endpoint or wire the producer to the refresh workflow and populate sleeper_id/asset_type. Whichever is chosen, stamp generated_at age on the response.

findings.title: One rostered player is absent from the board and from all three Sleeper identity maps while still appearing on his team's roster lists
findings.claimUnderTest: sleeper.playerIds / sleeper.idToPlayer / sleeper.positions are the identity maps for the league's rostered players.
findings.observed: Team 'Ed' carries Sleeper id 7058 in both teams[].players (as 'Jaylinn Hawkins') and teams[].playerIds, but 7058 is absent from sleeper.idToPlayer, sleeper.playerIds and sleeper.positions (all 937 entries), and has no row in playersArray. Verified against the live Sleeper directory (read-only GET api.sleeper.app/v1/players/nfl): 7058 = Jaylinn Hawkins, SS/DB, BAL, status Active. fantasyProsIdp.csv ranks him 181, so at least one source prices him. He is therefore an owned asset with no value, no position and no id->name resolution on any surface. He is the only such case (1 of 666 rostered assets).

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json')); s=d['sleeper']; b={str(r['playerId']) for r in d['playersArray'] if r.get('playerId')}; print([(t['name'],i) for t in s['teams'] for i in t['playerIds'] if str(i) not in b]); print('in idToPlayer:', '7058' in s['idToPlayer'])"
reproduction.expected: [] and True
reproduction.actual: [('Ed', '7058')] and False

numericProof.formula: orphans = |{sid in any team.playerIds : sid not in idToPlayer}|

findings.userImpact: Team Ed's roster value on /rosters and /league omits one IDP asset entirely, and no surface says a player was dropped.
findings.whatWorks: The remaining 665 rostered assets round-trip name->id->name with zero failures, and playerIds/idToPlayer/positions are all exactly 937 entries with no name claimed by two ids.
findings.rootCause: The identity maps are rebuilt from board rows after the blend (Dynasty Scraper.py:4837-4840), so a rostered player who never reaches the board is erased from the maps that ownership resolution reads.
findings.requiredRepair: Seed the rebuilt maps from the roster pass rather than replacing them, so rostered-but-unpriced assets keep an id->name entry and can be rendered as 'owned, unpriced'.

findings.title: The Sleeper name->id map is written with no collision guard while the sibling position map three lines above has one
findings.claimUnderTest: The in-line comment at Dynasty Scraper.py:1238-1242 states the collision policy: 'Name collision across universes (e.g. DJ Turner WR vs DJ Turner II CB both clean to "DJ Turner"). Drop the entry entirely - having no position is safer than tagging the row with the wrong family.'
findings.observed: That policy is applied to position_map only. Three lines earlier, player_id_map[cn] = sid and id_to_player[sid] = cn are written unconditionally on the same cleaned-name key. When two rostered players clean to one name, the second silently overwrites the first's Sleeper id in player_id_map, and id_to_player maps two ids onto one name - the exact asymmetry the comment argues against, on the exact example it names. Measured on the live block: 937/937/937 entries, 0 round-trip failures, 0 names claimed by more than one id - so the path is inert TODAY, and the position map's drop policy is doing the protective work by accident.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,collections; s=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json'))['sleeper']; print(len(s['playerIds']), len(s['idToPlayer']), len(s['positions'])); print('roundtrip failures:', sum(1 for n,i in s['playerIds'].items() if s['idToPlayer'].get(str(i))!=n)); print({k:v for k,v in collections.Counter(s['idToPlayer'].values()).items() if v>1})"
reproduction.expected: equal counts, 0 round-trip failures, {} - which is what happens today
reproduction.actual: 937 937 937 / 0 / {} - inert today, but unguarded by construction

numericProof.formula: len(playerIds) == len(idToPlayer) holds iff no two rostered players share a cleaned name

findings.userImpact: None observed today. On the next roster that adds a name twin (the comment names DJ Turner WR vs DJ Turner II CB as a real case), one of the two loses his Sleeper id and inherits the other's ownership on every ID-first surface.

priorFinding.note: A24-F05 documents the same class in src/pool/builder.py. This is a second, independent instance in Dynasty Scraper.py that no prior finding names, and it sits three lines from a comment stating the correct policy for its sibling map.

findings.whatWorks: position_map's collision policy is correct and does fire (the scraper prints a 'Dropped N colliding position entries' summary).
findings.rootCause: The guard was added to one of three maps written in the same loop body.
findings.requiredRepair: Apply the same drop-on-collision rule to player_id_map/id_to_player, or key all three on (cleanName, position) as src/identity/matcher.py already does.

findings.title: Terminal re-derives each row's Sleeper ID by lowercased display name even though every row already carries playerId - verified correct on the live payload
findings.claimUnderTest: terminal.py:191-196: 'The live pipeline emits playersArray WITHOUT _sleeperId on each row - that field only lives on the legacy players dict. When playersArray is populated we backfill each row with the _sleeperId from the matching dict entry.'
findings.observed: Accurate about _sleeperId, but the rows DO carry the same value under playerId (data_contract.py:8790 maps _sleeperId -> playerId), and neither _players_array nor _build_sleeper_id_lookup looks at it - both key exclusively on lowercased displayName. Ran _players_array against the live full and app contracts: 1,092 rows, 937 _sleeperId recovered, 937 rows carrying playerId, and 0 rows where a playerId was present but the name join failed. The name join is correct today because both surfaces are minted from the same build and their display names are byte-identical. Recorded as verified, with the note that it is a name join standing in for an ID already on the row.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys,json;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.api import terminal as t;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json'));r=t._players_array(d);print(len(r), sum(1 for x in r if x.get('_sleeperId')), sum(1 for x in r if x.get('playerId')), sum(1 for x in r if x.get('playerId') and not x.get('_sleeperId')))"

numericProof.formula: failures = |{row : row.playerId set and name-join produced no _sleeperId}|

findings.userImpact: None today.

priorFinding.note: Recorded as a verified negative: the name join works on the live payload.

findings.whatWorks: Full 937/937 recovery on both the full and app views, with zero failures.
findings.rootCause: The helper predates the playerId stamp and was never updated.
findings.requiredRepair: Prefer row['playerId'] and keep the name join only as a fallback - a one-line change that removes a name join from a hot path.

findings.title: Per-source name-join coverage measured on the live board: 17 of 21 sources join above 92%, but fantasyNavigatorSf loses 40% and draftSharksIdp 22% of their rows
findings.claimUnderTest: The enrichment cascade's docstring claims exact -> alias-aware -> position-aware fallback resolves cross-source drift.
findings.observed: Measured join rate per source against the live 1,092-key board: ktc 99.8%, ktcSfTep 99.8%, idpTradeCalc 99.9%, dlfIdp/idpShow/fantasyProsFitzmaurice/dlfRookieSf/dlfRookieIdp 100%, dlfSf 99.6%, dynastyNerdsSfTep 99.7%, otcffbSf 99.4%, dynastyDaddySf 99.5%, fantasyCalc 98.8%, fantasyProsIdp 96.8%, pfkDynasty 96.0%, flockFantasySf 94.8%, yahooBoone 92.0%, draftSharks 92.5%, flockFantasySfRookies 90.5%, fantasyProsSf 87.8%, draftSharksIdp 78.0%, fantasyNavigatorSf 60.0%. Independently reproduced by the repo's own scripts/audit_identity_matches.py to within 1 row on every source. Crucially, the misses are NOT identity failures: 455 distinct canonical keys appear in some CSV and in no board row at all, and spot checks (Maxwell Hairston, Benjamin Morrison, Christian Wilkins, Mason Rudolph, Tyrod Taylor, Odell Beckham) confirm those players have no board row under any spelling. The enrichment cascade only fills existing rows; it never creates one. 37 of the 455 are covered by 3 or more sources. Re-measured independently on the live contract and reproduced the same figures (fantasyProsSf 87.8% vs the doc's 99.1%, flockFantasySfRookies 90.5%), and added the diagnosis A24-F26 does not make: the misses are absent-from-pool, not mis-joined.

findings.whatWorks: POSITION_ALIASES (21 entries in src/utils/name_clean.py) covers every position token any live source emits (QB RB WR TE DE DT DL LB S CB DB) with no unmapped values, and canonical_position_group routes each to the right family.
findings.rootCause: n/a - measurement.
findings.requiredRepair: n/a. If the 37 multi-source absentees are wanted on the board, that is a pool-builder change, not an identity change.

findings.title: Every /rankings page load silently POSTs tep_multiplier=1.15, which bypasses the ADR-015 TE-basis curve — the rendered board under-prices 82 TEs by up to 21.2% and disagrees with GET /api/data on 627 ranks, while every server-side engine keeps pricing from /api/data
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'TE rows from non-TEP sources are lifted onto the basis the board is anchored on via convert_te_value(from_basis="base", to_basis="tepp") — KTC's own measured uplift, 1.209 at the top of the board rising toward 2.05 down it. Replaces a flat 1.15 that sat below the entire observed range.' And frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:2025-2028: 'Default path (no overrides) ... the backend will derive tep_multiplier ... so the frontend doesn't need to POST anything.'
findings.observed: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier = 1.15 is a finite number, and tepMultiplierIsCustomized() returns true for ANY finite number. So `customized` is true on every session including a browser with no localStorage at all. Measured in Chromium after `localStorage.removeItem('next_settings_v2')`: the very first request /rankings makes is POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta with body {"tep_multiplier":1.15}. The backend then sets tep_multiplier_is_override=True (tepMultiplierSource:'override'), and data_contract.py:6939 `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:` skips the te_basis_conversion block entirely — the flag is ON and the curve is loadable, it is simply never entered. Result: the board a user reads is a different board from the one GET /api/data serves and every server-side engine prices from. 8/8 sampled DOM cells reproduce the tep=1.15 delta payload exactly and none reproduce /api/data.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data -o /tmp/base-full.json; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/rankings/overrides?view=delta' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tep_multiplier":1.15}' -o /tmp/delta-tep115.json; .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W07/te_divergence.py; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/waiver/faab-recommend -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"addPlayerName":"Brevin Jordan","budgetRemaining":100}'
reproduction.expected: The board rendered on /rankings and the board every engine prices from are the same board; a TE's value is one number site-wide.
reproduction.actual: 135 rows differ in value (82 TE, 50 PICK, 3 other), 627 rows differ in canonicalConsensusRank, 654 in canonicalTierId. Brevin Jordan renders as 1,243 on /rankings (DOM-verified) while /api/waiver/faab-recommend answers resolvedAddValue: 1519.0 for the same player in the same session. Three TEs priced by /api/data (Grant Calcaterra 1340, Josh Oliver 1405, Thomas Fidone 1392) fall out of the rendered board's ranked set entirely and display as value 0.

numericProof.formula: pctUnderstated = 100 * (1 - renderedValue / apiDataValue)

findings.userImpact: A user opens /rankings, reads a tight-end's value, and trades or bids on it. The number is up to 21% lower than the value the site's own FAAB recommender, trade suggester, arbitrage finder and terminal are using for the same player at the same moment, and nothing on screen says the two disagree — /settings positively asserts the opposite by labelling this state 'Default 1.15x'. The direction is systematic: the flat 1.15 sits below the entire measured TE-basis range, so users sell tight ends cheap.

priorFinding.note: Prior stated the mechanism (default settings force the override path, making ADR-015 unreachable). Independently rediscovered here and extended with runtime proof: browser network capture on a cleared localStorage, DOM-vs-payload identity on 8/8 players, and the cross-surface divergence against a live /api/waiver/faab-recommend response. Also quantifies the collateral 627-row rank and 654-row tier drift the prior finding did not measure.

findings.whatWorks: The backend half is correct and deliberate: an operator-typed tep_multiplier SHOULD bypass a measured curve, and data_contract.py documents exactly that. The delta payload is faithful (0 field mismatches vs view=full across 1,092 rows). The defect is entirely that the frontend sends an operator decision nobody made.
findings.rootCause: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier is the literal 1.15 rather than the null 'auto' sentinel the backend contract defines, and tepMultiplierIsCustomized() cannot distinguish 'the user typed 1.15' from 'this is the shipped default'.
findings.requiredRepair: Set SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier back to null (the documented 'derive from league' sentinel) and drop the readSettings() migration that rewrites null to 1.15; the /settings slider should write a number only on an actual user edit. Then re-verify that a cleared-localStorage load fires no override POST and that /rankings matches GET /api/data row-for-row.
findings.dependencies: Interacts with W07-F002 (the /settings UI labelling) and W07-F008 (the client-side overlay path this also strands).

findings.title: /settings renders the forced TE-premium override as 'Default 1.15x' and its 'Reset to default' button writes the override, so no reachable UI state produces the non-override board
findings.claimUnderTest: settings/page.jsx:246-252 — 'Treat the explicit default value ... as "default" so the UI doesn't render the default as a Custom override.'
findings.observed: tepIsDefault is true for tepMultiplier === 1.15, so the slider prints 'Default 1.15x' and the CustomMixBadge stays quiet — while the wire body carries tep_multiplier: 1.15 and the backend stamps tepMultiplierSource: 'override'. The 'Reset to default' button calls update('tepMultiplier', 1.15), i.e. resetting to default WRITES an explicit override. useSettings.readSettings() additionally coerces a stored null (the real 'auto' sentinel) to 1.15 and sets tepDefaultV3Applied so the coercion is one-way. There is no click path in the product that produces tepMultiplier === null.

reproduction.command: PW_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W07/probes/w07_probe4.py
reproduction.expected: A session that has never touched the TE slider posts no tep_multiplier, and /settings' 'Default' label describes the board actually being served.
reproduction.actual: With localStorage removed, the first POST is {"tep_multiplier":1.15}; the backend response carries tepMultiplierSource:'override' while tepMultiplierDerived is also 1.15, so the response looks identical to the default path and the UI has no signal that the curve was skipped.

numericProof.formula: UI asserts isDefault iff tepMultiplier === 1.15; backend asserts isOverride iff the key is present

findings.userImpact: A user who wants the platform's designed TE valuation cannot get it, and is told they already have it. Anyone diagnosing the TE discrepancy from the UI is sent the wrong way: both the slider caption and rankingsOverride.isCustomized:false say 'nothing is overridden'.

priorFinding.note: Independently rediscovered. Adds that rankingsOverride.isCustomized comes back false on the override path too, so the backend's own response cannot be used to detect the state either.

findings.whatWorks: tepNativeMultiplier defaults to null and behaves correctly — it is the working shape the tepMultiplier knob should copy.
findings.rootCause: Two different definitions of 'default': the UI's (value equals the shipped constant) and the backend's (key absent).
findings.requiredRepair: Make null the only 'default' state in the UI as well as on the wire; 'Reset to default' should clear the key, not write 1.15.

findings.title: 222 rows on the live board display a client-invented ordinal in the # column, and CLAUDE.md's stated bound for that fallback is factually wrong — the backend's board stops at rank 740, never reaching the 800 limit the doc cites
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'buildRows assigns a display ordinal computedConsensusRank = i + 1 ... and uses it for r.rank only when the backend stamped no canonicalConsensusRank on that row. In practice that is players past the backend's OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT (800) — rows the backend deliberately left unranked.'
findings.observed: On the live 1,092-row contract the deepest backend-stamped rank is 740; OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT (800) is never reached, so the doc's stated population does not exist. The rows that actually take the fallback are the 239 non-pick rows the backend refused to price at all — canonicalConsensusRank null AND rankDerivedValue null AND canonicalTierId null AND confidenceLabel 'None - unranked'. After the rankings page's own filters, 222 of them render with a client-invented # in the range 854-1092. Reproduced in the browser: Austin Ekeler renders '#865', AJ Dillon '#858', Alexander Mattison '#860', Arian Smith '#864' — visually identical to Josh Allen's backend-stamped '#1'. The mechanism claim ('a backend-stamped rank always wins') IS true and was verified: Trey Lance #673 and T.J. Watt #185 reproduce the backend stamp exactly.

reproduction.command: PW_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W07/probes/w07_probe2.py
reproduction.expected: Rows the backend declined to rank show no rank number (the treatment picks already get: r.rank = null).
reproduction.actual: 222 rows show a fabricated ordinal indistinguishable from a real rank; the deepest is #1092 for a player with no value.

numericProof.formula: fabricated = rows where canonicalConsensusRank is null AND assetClass != 'pick' AND pos is renderable; ordinal = sortIndex + 1 over all materialized rows

findings.userImpact: A user sorting or filtering the deep board reads '#865 Austin Ekeler, RB115' and treats it as the platform's assessment. It is an array index. The board has no opinion on this player at all — the value cell shows 0 — yet the rank cell asserts a precise position among 1,092 assets.

priorFinding.note: Prior counted 216 and framed the ordinals as 'array indices that count unranked picks'. Independently reproduced at 222 on today's contract and refined: picks are correctly excluded from the fallback (r.rank = null for assetClass 'pick'), but they still occupy sort slots so the ordinals skip. The new part is that CLAUDE.md's stated bound for the fallback is measurably false — the 800 limit is never reached and the affected rows are unpriced, not merely deep.

findings.whatWorks: The precedence rule is correct and verified: a backend-stamped canonicalConsensusRank always wins, and picks correctly render no rank. The fail-fast on a payload with zero rank stamps is real code and is reachable.
findings.rootCause: The fallback branch at dynasty-data.js:1402 treats 'backend left this unranked' and 'legacy payload with no stamps' as the same case.
findings.requiredRepair: Give unpriced non-pick rows the same treatment as picks — r.rank = null — and let the # column render the existing '-' placeholder. computedConsensusRank can stay as an internal sort key.
findings.dependencies: W07-F004 depends on this: tierLabel and the positional-rank map are both derived from r.rank.

findings.title: The board fabricates a tier, a positional rank, a confidence badge and an actionable BUY/SELL verdict for the 222 players it declines to price
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'buildRows is a pure materializer ... it trusts backend stamps verbatim.' board-sections.jsx: 'these render backend stamps verbatim (no ranking math client-side).'
findings.observed: For Austin Ekeler the backend stamps canonicalTierId: null, positionRank: null, confidenceLabel: 'None - unranked', confidenceBucket: 'none', marketGapDirection: 'none', edgeSignal: null, rankDerivedValue: null. The rendered row shows TIER 'Tier 10', POS 'RB 115', CONFIDENCE 'Low', VALUE '0'. Alexander Mattison renders EDGE 'SELL' and AJ Dillon renders EDGE 'BUY'. Each is client-computed: tierLabel() falls through to rankBasedTierLabel(row.rank) — a tier derived from the invented ordinal of W07-F003; positionRankByName (page.jsx:716) re-derives QB1/RB115 client-side from the same ordinals; marketAction()/marketEdge() recompute a retail-vs-consensus verdict from effectiveSourceRanks without ever consulting the backend's marketGapDirection.

reproduction.command: PW_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W07/probes/w07_probe2.py  # then: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;c=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W07/base-full.json'));i={p['displayName']:p for p in c['playersArray']};print(i['Austin Ekeler'])"
reproduction.expected: A row the pipeline declined to price shows no tier, no positional rank, no confidence grade and no buy/sell verdict.
reproduction.actual: Rendered: #865 / Tier 10 / RB 115 / Low / '0' / '-' for Ekeler; AJ Dillon renders EDGE 'BUY' and Alexander Mattison EDGE 'SELL' on rows with rankDerivedValue null.

numericProof.formula: tierLabel(row) = canonicalTierId ?? rankBasedTierId(row.rank); row.rank = computedConsensusRank for unpriced rows

findings.userImpact: The board tells a user to BUY a player it has assigned no value, and files him in 'Tier 10' as if that were a modelled cluster. A manager screening for buy-low targets deep on the board is served pure sort-order artefacts as trade advice.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A01-F02/F03 cover contradictory edge thresholds in general. The specific defect here — an actionable BUY/SELL, a tier and a positional rank emitted for rows the backend explicitly refused to price — is new, and it is downstream of PRIOR-A01-F01 (confirmed as W07-F003) rather than a restatement of it.

findings.whatWorks: The VALUE cell is honest-ish for these rows (it renders 0 with a '-' grade rather than inventing a number), and the CONSENSUS cell correctly renders '-'.
findings.rootCause: Every derived display field keys off row.rank, which W07-F003 populates with an invented ordinal; and marketEdge() was written against per-source ranks rather than against the backend's own marketGapDirection stamp.
findings.requiredRepair: Fix W07-F003 first (r.rank = null for unpriced rows) — that alone corrects tier and positional rank. Separately, gate marketAction() on rankDerivedValue being non-null, or key it off the backend's marketGapDirection.

findings.title: The rankings-override delta is 3.74 MB / 342 KB gzipped, not the ~1.25 MB / ~100 KB CLAUDE.md documents, and W07-F001 puts that POST on the critical path of every page load for every user
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Production payload drops from ~4 MB to ~1.25 MB uncompressed, and to ~100 KB over the wire with FastAPI's GZipMiddleware.'
findings.observed: Measured on the live 1,092-row contract: view=full is 11,271,885 bytes and view=delta is 3,739,098 bytes (ratio 0.332), gzipped over the wire 349,679 bytes. Both documented absolute figures are understated ~3x. 2.20 MB of the 3.74 MB delta — 59% — is the sourceRankMeta block, shipped for all 1,092 rows on every request. The pinning test (test_delta_byte_size_is_bounded) asserts delta_bytes < 55,000 against a toy fixture and delta/full < 0.60, so neither production absolute size nor a 3x drift trips it. This matters more than doc drift because W07-F001 makes this POST fire on every page load of every session, so it is no longer a customized-session cost.

findings.title: The /trade calculator never sums the canonical board: the frontend posts an explicit tep_multiplier=1.15 on every load, which disables the ADR-015 TE basis conversion and reprices 129 of 809 players by up to -21.2%
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md ADR-015: TE rows from non-TEP sources are lifted via te_premium.convert_te_value using KTC's measured uplift (1.209 at the top rising toward 2.05), replacing 'a flat 1.15 that sat below the entire observed range'; the feature ships flag-ON. CLAUDE.md also states 'an explicit operator slider value bypasses the curve regardless' — but does not note that the frontend always sends one. useSettings.js additionally claims tepMultiplier=null means 'auto from league / inherit from backend'.
findings.observed: data_contract.py gates the whole basis conversion behind `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:`. `useSettings.js` SETTINGS_DEFAULTS sets tepMultiplier: 1.15 (a finite number), and readSettings() actively coerces null/1.0/1.25 back to 1.15 on first read. tepMultiplierIsCustomized() returns true for any finite number, so fetchDynastyData takes the override path and POSTs {"tep_multiplier":1.15} on EVERY page load. Captured live from the browser on /trade: `POST /api/rankings/overrides?view=delta {"tep_multiplier":1.15}`. The response reports tepMultiplier 1.15, tepMultiplierDefault 1.15, tepMultiplierDerived 1.15, isCustomized false — identical declared parameters to the base contract — but tepMultiplierSource flips 'default' -> 'override' and 129 of 809 players get different values. The ADR-015 curve is therefore unreachable from the product: no user-facing path produces the board the backend calls canonical.

reproduction.actual: 129 of 809 differ. Tyler Conklin 1450 -> 1142 (-21.2%), Josh Cuevas 1541 -> 1215 (-21.2%), Sam LaPorta 5222 -> 5021 (-3.8%). 89 players >5%, 54 >10%. Confirmed in the DOM: /trade renders Sam LaPorta at 5,021, /api/dynasty-data says 5,222.

A user trading a TE gives one away ~20% too cheap (or overpays to acquire one) on a board the app cannot be configured to leave — clearing the setting is undone by the readSettings() migration. The measured TE-basis feature the repo shipped and flagged ON is dead in production.

priorFinding.note: No area-2 prior finding covers the TEP override path or the base-vs-override board divergence. Adjacent but distinct from PRIOR-A02-F11 (which is about KTC constants being fed our blended values, not about which blend).

findings.rootCause: src/api/data_contract.py:6939 gates te_basis_conversion on `not tep_multiplier_is_override`, and the frontend's default settings make every request an override. The gate was written for 'the operator moved the slider'; nothing checks whether the posted value equals the derived default, and the frontend has no 'unset' state because readSettings() rewrites null back to 1.15.

findings.title: The Value Adjustment tooltip tells the user the bonus goes to 'the side with fewer pieces', but 46.7% of fired VAs go to a side with equal or MORE pieces
findings.claimUnderTest: SideCard renders title="Consolidation / roster-spot premium: the side with fewer pieces frees a roster spot, so KTC-style math adds this bonus on top of the raw total." The same file's own algorithm docstring contradicts it: 'KTC's algorithm is symmetric: equal-count trades (e.g. 2v2 stud-vs-pile) fire VA when one side has bigger studs.'
findings.observed: ktcAdjustPackage awards the VA on raw_adj INTENSITY (e/team1Total vs a/team2Total — i.e. which side's value is concentrated in bigger studs), not on piece count. Piece count only enters through the progressive nerf and the 1v1 suppression. Over 50,000 random 1-4 vs 1-4 trades built from the live board, the VA fired 21,610 times: 11,524 (53.3%) to the side with fewer pieces, 6,815 (31.5%) on equal counts, 3,271 (15.1%) to the side with MORE pieces. Concrete live case: A=[Bijan Robinson 9706, Tyjae Spears 2121, Jessie Bates 1707, Kyle Hamilton 3062] (4 pieces) vs B=[Jadarian Price 4286, Dak Prescott 5519, 2028 Late 1st 4079] (3 pieces) -> VA 3,815 credited to A, the side with MORE pieces. findings.title: Adding a positive-value asset to your side can lower your side's total and flip the verdict against you — the fairness gap is non-monotonic in 1.1-1.9% of trades
findings.claimUnderTest: adjustedSideTotals returns `adjusted = raw + adjustment`, and TradeMeter/verdictFromGap render the verdict off `adjustedA - adjustedB`. The implicit contract of a trade calculator is that adding value to a side improves that side's position.
findings.observed: Because the VA is a discontinuous function of the piece SET (1v1 suppression, the 3.3% display floor, the progressive nerf, and the branch switch on raw_adj intensity), adding one positive-value asset to side A can reduce A's adjusted total. Over 40,000 random 1-3 vs 1-3 trades from the live board, 772 (1.93%) got WORSE for A after adding a real asset to A; 27 of those crossed a meter-verdict label boundary. Restricting to multi-asset shapes only (2-3 per side, so the 1v1 suppression rule cannot explain it), 687 of 60,000 (1.15%) still violate. Live example (all values are live board values): A=[2026 Pick 1.04 5320, Jadarian Price 4286, Dont'e Thornton 1509] vs B=[T.J. Hockenson 3107, 2026 Pick 2.09 2846, Kaden Elliss 1869]; gap +4903 with a 1,610 VA on A. Add Boye Mafe (1,235 board points) to A -> A's VA drops to 0 and the gap FALLS to +4528. Verdict-flipping example: A=[Daiyan Henley 1923] vs B=[2028 Late 2nd 2785], gap -862 = SLIGHT EDGE; add Omar Speights (894) to A -> gap -1219 = UNFAIR.

reproduction.command: cd docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W08 && node mono2.mjs && node mono3.mjs
reproduction.expected: For every trade T and every asset x with value(x) > 0: gap(A+x, B) >= gap(A, B). Violations: 0.
reproduction.actual: 772 / 40,000 (1.93%) for 1-3 per side; 687 / 60,000 (1.15%) for 2-3 per side; 27 verdict-label flips.

findings.userImpact: The user follows the page's own signal — 'you are behind, add something' — adds a real asset, and the verdict moves further against them with no explanation. On the 27 measured flips the badge goes from SLIGHT EDGE to UNFAIR (or UNFAIR to LOPSIDED) as a direct result of the user giving MORE. They will then remove a good asset or demand more back, which is the wrong negotiating move.

priorFinding.note: F10 framed this as a balancer-selection bug ('sized against a VA-inclusive gap but selected by raw value') and illustrated it with a hand-built 1-for-many shape. Confirmed and generalised: the non-monotonicity is a property of adjustedSideTotals itself, independent of findBalancers, and I measured its rate on the live board (1.15% for multi-asset shapes where the 1v1 suppression cannot be the cause) plus 27 verdict-label flips. F10's proposed cause (balancers select on raw value) is necessary but not sufficient — no selection rule fixes a non-monotonic objective.

findings.whatWorks: The gap is exactly A/B symmetric (see W08-F009), so the non-monotonicity is not an ordering artifact.
findings.rootCause: The VA is folded into the side totals (`adjusted = raw + adjustment`) and then differenced, but ktcAdjustPackage is a step function of the piece multiset with three discontinuities (1v1 suppression, the |value|/(totalA+totalB) < 0.033 display floor, and the branch switch on h vs y). KTC itself displays the VA as an advisory 'add this much to even it out' badge, not as an addend to a side total — folding it into the meter is what turns the discontinuity into a verdict flip.
findings.requiredRepair: Either stop folding the VA into `adjusted` and render it as KTC does (an advisory line beside a raw-total verdict), or clamp: compute the VA, and if adding an asset to a side would reduce that side's adjusted total, hold the previous VA and surface a note. The first is smaller and matches the source the port is faithful to.
findings.dependencies: Compounds with PRIOR-A02-F02 (absolute fairness bands), which is what makes the 27 label flips reachable at small gaps.

findings.title: Pick original-owner identity is discarded before it reaches the trade calculator: 53 of 216 league picks collapse onto a duplicate name, and the duplicate guard then makes them untradeable
findings.claimUnderTest: The trade calculator can represent a league team's real pick holdings. CLAUDE.md's draft-capital section treats pick ownership as real Sleeper-derived data.
findings.observed: The contract's sleeper.teams[].pickDetails carries {season, round, slot, original_roster_id, owner_roster_id, label} for every pick — original_roster_id IS present and correct. The trade page reads only team.picks (the flat label array), where all of Jason's eight 2027 firsts are the identical string '2027 1st'. resolvePickRow maps every one of them to the tier-centre row '2027 Mid 1st' @ 5,606. teamRosterNames() then returns a Set, and addToSide() refuses any name already in the trade (`allTradeNames.has(row.name)`). Net effect measured on the live league: Jason holds 62 picks that resolve to 18 distinct row names; the league holds 216 picks that resolve to 163 distinct names — 53 picks are unrepresentable. A trade of two 2027 firsts cannot be built at all, and a rebuilding team's first is priced identically to a contender's.

reproduction.actual: 216 -> 163 distinct names (53 collapsed). Jason: 62 -> 18. His eight 2027 firsts (original_roster_id 1,2,3,6,8,9,10,12) all become '2027 Mid 1st' @ 5,606.

findings.userImpact: A manager holding multiple firsts in the same year (the single most common consolidation-trade setup in dynasty) cannot model the trade. findings.userImpact: A user who flips to 'Raw' to sanity-check a mixed offense/IDP trade gets a verdict that disagrees with the default one by 25 percentage points and names the other winner.
