findings.title: src/nfl_data/realized_points.py disagrees with the league host on 36% of player-weeks: it never reads the six reception-distance rules, maps pass_int/pass_sack/fum_lost to nflverse columns that no longer exist, and has no kicker scoring at all
findings.claimUnderTest: src/league_comparison/scoring_engine.py:6 — 'compute_weekly_points ... is already the single source of truth for Sleeper-format fantasy scoring'. CLAUDE.md — BDVM's baseline is 'realized nflverse PPG under the league's exact scoring'.
findings.observed: Scored 636 real 2025 player-weeks (nflverse rows) against the same 636 Sleeper host stat lines under the SAME live dynasty_main scoring_settings. Only 406 (63.8%) agree within 0.011. Three independent causes, each confirmed by decomposing individual players: (1) rec_0_4/rec_5_9/rec_10_19/rec_20_29/rec_30_39/rec_40p appear in neither _SIMPLE_KEYS nor the threshold-bonus list, costing 157.03 points across 197 rows — Stefon Diggs 2025 wk5 exact 30.100 vs realized 23.400, delta -6.700 = 0.34+4.02+2.34 exactly. (2) _SIMPLE_KEYS maps pass_int->'interceptions', pass_sack->'sacks', fum_lost->'fumbles_lost'; the 2025 unified nflverse release names them passing_interceptions, sacks_suffered and fumbles_lost_total, so stat_row.get returns None -> _num -> 0.0 and the key is skipped. Patrick Mahomes wk14 exact 0.823 vs realized 14.823, delta exactly +14.000 = 3 INT x 4.00 + 2 sacks x 1.00. Across the sample these three penalties are worth 208 points that are never charged. (3) No kicker key is read at all (fgm_yds 0.07, xpm 2.31, xpmiss -3.15, six fgmiss_* bands) although K is a starting slot; every kicker scores 0.000 (33/33 rows wrong, mean -9.251). Per-group agreement: IDP 312/350 (89.1%, mean -0.034 — this path is essentially correct), other 66/71, WR 11/64, TE 10/48, RB 4/32, QB 3/38 (mean +6.533), K 0/33 (mean -9.251).

reproduction.command: bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W18/repro.sh   # section R5
reproduction.expected: 636/636 agree within 0.011 (the tolerance src/league_intel/scorer.py's own docstring sets)
reproduction.actual: 406/636 agree; QB mean +6.533, K mean -9.251, WR mean -1.558

inputs.reference: src/league_intel/scorer.score_stat_line, itself validated 1339/1339 vs Sleeper players_points

numericProof.formula: delta = compute_weekly_points(nflverse_row) - score_stat_line(sleeper_stat_line); agreement = count(|delta| <= 0.011)

findings.userImpact: The direction is systematic, not random: QBs are over-scored by ~6.5 pts/week and pass-catchers under-scored by 0.8-1.6 pts/week, so any fundamental value built on this engine tilts the board toward QBs and away from WR/TE/RB. On /rankings the 'Fund gap' column and on /bdvm the entire value board are derived from it; on /league-comparison the positional-balance verdict a user reads to decide whether their league over-pays QBs is computed from the engine that over-pays QBs.

priorFinding.note: Confirms the reception-band half exactly (6 rules, WR most affected) and extends it with two causes that audit did not report: three dead nflverse column mappings worth +208 pts of uncharged QB penalties, and the complete absence of kicker scoring in a league that starts a K. Also partially confirms PRIOR-A24-F19 and refutes the implication in PRIOR-A22-F02 that IDP is the broken half — measured, IDP is the ONE group this engine gets right.

findings.whatWorks: The IDP path is correct and well-defended: the _SCORING_KEY_ALIASES derivation from sleeper_ingest.KEY_ALIASES resolves idp_pass_def->idp_pd and idp_qb_hit->idp_hit, _tackle_view reconstructs gamebook solo from the post-2025 columns, and the group agrees with the host at 89.1% with mean signed error -0.034.
findings.rootCause: realized_points is an allow-list engine keyed on nflverse column names, in a codebase that also contains a scoring-key-agnostic dot-product engine (src/league_intel/scorer.py) that is provably exact. The allow-list silently degrades in two ways — a live scoring rule with no entry, and an entry whose column was renamed — and _num(None) -> 0.0 makes both indistinguishable from 'the player did nothing'.
findings.requiredRepair: Add rec_0_4..rec_40p (nflverse publishes no reception-depth split, so they must come from src/nfl_data/reception_depth.py or be reported as uncovered, not silently zero); repoint pass_int/pass_sack/fum_lost at passing_interceptions/sacks_suffered/fumbles_lost_total via the existing candidate-tuple mechanism; add the kicker family. Structurally: make the engine assert that every NONZERO key in the league's scoring_settings is either mapped or explicitly declared uncoverable, and surface the uncovered set on the payload (src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py already exists for this and is not consulted at scoring time).
findings.dependencies: None. src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py already enumerates the gap.

findings.title: /api/player/{id}/realized returns reason:'unmapped_player' for every player because it reads a players directory key the sleeper block does not have, and the PlayerPopup that now calls it 404s on the Next origin
findings.claimUnderTest: server.py:11213 — 'What kept the row-filter bug below invisible was not the flag but the absence of a caller: nothing in the frontend requests this.' The 2026-07-27 fix comment at :11271-11288 claims the endpoint now matches rows correctly.
findings.observed: Two independent failures, both live. (a) server.py:11264 does players_dir = sleeper_block.get('players') or sleeper_block.get('playerDict'). The contract's sleeper block has neither key — its actual keys are idToPlayer, playerIds, positions, rosterPositions, scoringSettings, leagueSettings, teams, trades, waivers, tradeWindow*, overlay*. players_dir is therefore always None, unified_mapper.resolve_player(None, ...) returns None, and the route short-circuits to reason:'unmapped_player' with an empty weeks list for every player id — verified for 5849 (Kyler Murray), 9756, 10891 and 6794. The weekly stats DO load (19,421 nflverse rows for 2025 in this container), which is why the response is 'unmapped_player' and not 'no_stats_available'. Even if a directory were passed, idToPlayer is {id: name} and carries no gsis_id, so the `not resolved.gsis_id` guard would still fire. (b) The claim that nothing calls it is now false: frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:397 fetches /api/player/{id}/realized — but there is no bridge route under frontend/app/api/player/, so on the production origin (:3000) the request returns HTTP 404 (an HTML page), res.ok is false, and the RealizedPointsSection silently renders nothing. (c) Separately, line 11234 reads latest_contract_data['sleeper'] directly rather than the league it just resolved at :11229, so a non-default leagueKey would be scored with the loaded league's settings.

findings.title: refresh_snapshot's drift filter omits daily_waivers_last_ran, so a pure in-season bookkeeping counter reports as league-rule drift and writes a spurious dated snapshot
findings.claimUnderTest: src/league_intel/config.py:244-249 — 'Drift diffs are scoped to behavior-relevant payload fields ... so chatter (last_message_id etc.) never reads as drift', with _SETTINGS_NOISE_KEYS = {leg, last_scored_leg, last_report}.
findings.observed: Diffing the stored 2026-07-26 snapshot against the live host today produces exactly one settings difference: daily_waivers_last_ran 26 -> 4. findings.title: ADR-006's 'pure dot product, no stacking rules' claim independently reproduced against 1,339 host-scored player-weeks (max |delta| 0.005), and stacking answered on real host stat lines: pick-six charges -6.00, distance bonuses stack on the base reception, and one sack pays eight IDP categories
findings.claimUnderTest: src/league_intel/scorer.py:3-25 — 'a pure dot product over the keys shared between a player's weekly stat line and the league's scoring_settings ... No exclusions, no de-duplication, no special-casing ... reproduced Sleeper's own players_points exactly (|delta| <= 0.011) for 1,415 of 1,415 rostered player-weeks.'
findings.observed: Reproduced independently, not inherited. Fetched the 2025 predecessor league (1180092661344120832) with its own scoring_settings plus GET /v1/league/.../matchups/{5,9,14} for host-awarded players_points and GET /v1/stats/nfl/regular/2025/{5,9,14} for the raw stat lines. score_stat_line reproduces the host on 1,339 of 1,339 player-weeks with max |delta| = 0.005, inside the module's own 0.011 tolerance. Stacking, answered from host stat lines rather than from docs: (1) PICK-SIX STACKS — the host emits pass_int and pass_int_td on the same line (3 real cases, e.g. player 4046 wk5: pass_int 1.0, pass_int_td 1.0), so under 2026 rates a pick-six costs -4.00 AND -2.00 = -6.00. (2) RECEPTION-DISTANCE BONUSES STACK ON THE BASE RECEPTION — the buckets partition the receptions (rec_0_4 + rec_5_9 + rec_10_19 + rec_20_29 + rec_30_39 + rec_40p == rec) and are paid in addition to rec x 0.08; an 8-catch line at 1/3/3/0/1/0 scores 0.64 + 4.61 = 5.25 before yardage. (3) ONE SACK PAYS EVERYTHING APPLICABLE — 194 host lines carry idp_sack together with idp_sack_yd, idp_tkl_solo, idp_tkl_ast, idp_tkl_loss, idp_qb_hit and often idp_ff / idp_fum_rec. Worked case (player 4967, wk5, 2026 rates): ff 4.25 + fum_rec 3.19 + qb_hit 2.13 + sack 2.92 + sack_yd 1.111 + tkl_ast 0.80 + tkl_loss 4.25 + tkl_solo 1.33 = 19.981. The host also emits idp_tkl (combined), which carries no rate in this league, so solo+assist are not double-counted — a league that DID set idp_tkl would triple-count, and that would be Sleeper's behaviour too.

reproduction.expected: max |delta| <= 0.011 across all compared player-weeks
reproduction.actual: 1,339 player-weeks, max |delta| = 0.0050

findings.userImpact: None — this establishes which engine in the repo is correct, and therefore what every other engine must be measured against.

findings.title: The registry's dynasty_new entry is wrong against its own live host on every roster field it models, and models neither the WRRB_FLEX slot the league actually uses nor IR — and no test or snapshot covers it
findings.claimUnderTest: src/league_intel/config.py:10-14 — 'the registry stays the lightweight per-league pointer used for routing and roster-shape consumers ... The two must agree — tests/league_intel/test_registry_consumers.py pins that.' /api/leagues serves rosterSettings to the frontend as fact.
findings.observed: Fetched the live host for dynasty_new (1320092771247222784) read-only. Every roster field the registry models is wrong: rosterSize 24 vs 27 real slots; taxiSize 5 vs taxi_slots 3; starters FLEX 2 vs a host lineup of FLEX 1 + WRRB_FLEX 1. The registry has no vocabulary for WRRB_FLEX at all, so the second flex is served to the frontend as an RB/WR/TE slot when the host restricts it to RB/WR — a TE placed there is not a legal starter. reserve_slots 3 (this league DOES have IR, unlike dynasty_main) is not modelled anywhere. bestBall is absent from the entry and the host says best_ball 0, so the default happens to be right by luck. /api/leagues serves all of this verbatim. tests/league_intel/test_registry_consumers.py pins ONLY dynasty_main (its _registry_main helper selects key == 'dynasty_main'), and there is no config/league_intel snapshot for dynasty_new, so nothing in the 5,867-test suite compares this entry to anything.

reproduction.actual: registry rosterSize 24, taxiSize 5, starters {QB1,RB2,WR3,TE1,FLEX2,SFLEX1}; WRRB_FLEX and IR unmodelled

findings.userImpact: Every roster-shape consumer for this league is off: /rosters splits starters from bench using a 24-slot lineup against a 27-slot roster (3 real players fall off the end), the taxi squad is shown as 5 when it is 3, and a TE can be recommended into a slot the host will not let it start in.

priorFinding.note: The prior set covers dynasty_main's registry correction (test_registry_consumers.py's own docstring records it) but contains no finding that dynasty_new's entry was never given the same treatment.

findings.whatWorks: The registry loader, alias resolution and /api/leagues serialization are all correct — they faithfully serve whatever the file says. src/bdvm/league_config.py already prefers the contract's sleeper block over the registry and calls rosterSettings 'advisory and known to drift', which is the correct posture.
findings.rootCause: dynasty_new was added to the registry by hand and never validated against its own host; the test that would have caught it is hardcoded to dynasty_main and there is no snapshot for the second league.
findings.requiredRepair: Capture a config/league_intel snapshot for dynasty_new (config.py's snapshot machinery is per-league-id already), extend test_registry_consumers.py to loop over every registry entry instead of selecting dynasty_main, and add WRRB_FLEX / REC_FLEX and a reserveSize field to the registry's roster vocabulary (src/bdvm/league_config._FLEX_SLOTS already knows WRRB_FLEX and REC_FLEX; frontend/lib/starter-slots.js does not).

findings.title: Public trade letter grades silently drop 224 of 1,708 traded asset slots (13.1%) that the board cannot price — including 20 first-round-pick slots — and emit a confident 'Robbery'/'Fleeced' badge with no unpriced-asset disclosure anywhere on the payload or the page
findings.claimUnderTest: src/api/public_activity_valuation.py:70 says 'Returns 0.0 when no board value is available, which activity.build_section treats as "cannot grade this asset"'. src/trade/finder.py sets the house standard by counting omissions in metadata.assetsUnpricedByBoard.
findings.observed: sanitize_side_values keeps only strictly-positive values, so a 0.0 asset is dropped from BOTH the linear sum and the KTC value adjustment — it is treated as if it were never in the trade, not as 'cannot grade'. The grade is still emitted. Across the live 191-trade public feed 224/1708 asset slots price to 0.0: 156 pick slots and 68 player slots. 63/191 trades (33%) and 126/393 sides (32%) contain at least one. The dropped picks include 6x '2024 R1' and 14x '2025 R1' slots — first-round rookie picks that were the headline asset of their trade. No field on the payload and no element on activity.jsx records the omission.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python /tmp/w19_evidence.py   # writes docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W19/numeric-proof.json; requires /tmp/w19_contract_full.json from `curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w19.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data`
reproduction.expected: Either every traded asset carries a value, or the grade is suppressed / annotated when one does not
reproduction.actual: tradeGradeZeroPricedAssets = {totalByKind:{player:1238,pick:470}, zeroByKind:{pick:156,player:68}, tradesAffected:63/191, sidesAffected:126/393}; zeroPickLabels includes '2024 R1':6, '2025 R1':14, '2027 R5':6, '2029 R4':6

numericProof.formula: gotValue=sum(positive values); netAdjusted = netLinear + vaNet; pctGap = netAdjusted / max(got,gave) * 100 -> band table

findings.userImpact: On the public Trades tab, Jason is publicly graded 'D — Robbery' on transaction 1388782397222293506 while three of the five assets he received counted as nothing. A reader — including league members — treats the letter as a verdict on a manager's competence. 33% of the public trade history carries a grade computed on an incomplete asset set with no warning.

priorFinding.note: The specific mechanism the prior audit described (floor to 1.0, then pow(...,1.65)) is GONE — activity.py no longer computes the grade and _GRADE_ALPHA no longer exists. sanitize_side_values now drops zeros instead of flooring them. The defect class survives the rewrite: unpriceable assets still vanish silently and a confident grade is still emitted. Same relation applies to PRIOR-A21-F02.

findings.whatWorks: The grading arithmetic itself reproduces exactly: recomputing feed[0] through trade_grading.grade_trade_sides against the live private contract returns the identical served grades (Jason D, Ed A+, pctGap -27.866/+27.866). The scale bug the prior audit found is genuinely fixed.
findings.rootCause: The valuation callable conflates 'worth zero' with 'not on this board'. The 2026 board carries pick rows for 2026-2028 rounds 1-6 only; every 2024/2025 pick and every round >=5 future pick has no row, and dropping them is indistinguishable from a zero-value asset downstream.
findings.requiredRepair: Have the callable return None for 'unpriced' and 0.0 only for 'genuinely worthless'. Count unpriced assets per side, stamp `unpricedAssetCount` on the side, and suppress the grade (or badge it 'partial') when a side has any. This is exactly the posture src/trade/finder.py already ships as metadata.assetsUnpricedByBoard.

There is no jitter and no uncertainty: playoff_odds.py:639-642 substitutes a single-element pool [100.0] for owners with no scored weeks, and rng.choice over a one-element list is a point mass. numSims stays 10000 on the payload, and nothing marks the owners as unsimulated. The card is currently shadowed because useSettings.js:143 defaults useRosPowerRankings to true (LeagueClient.jsx:391 then renders RosPowerSection), but the /settings toggle at page.jsx:759 makes it one click reachable.

findings.title: VERIFIED POSITIVE — the public trade grader now uses the canonical linear-ratio + KTC-value-adjustment formula, and its served grades reproduce exactly; the prior audit's alpha=1.65 threshold-mismatch defect is gone from the tree
findings.claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A21-F01 / PRIOR-A03-F01: 'src/public_league/activity.py:118 total += pow(max(val, 1.0), _GRADE_ALPHA) with _GRADE_ALPHA = 1.65 (:49)' produces an alpha-transformed pct bucketed against linear-calibrated 3/8/15/25/40 cuts, so the same trade grades Fair on /trades and Robbery on /league.

findings.title: 'All-time' league records are actually a rolling PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS=3 window; it is correct only by coincidence today and will silently start truncating history at the 2027 season with no label change
findings.claimUnderTest: src/public_league/streaks.py documents longestWinStreaks/longestLossStreaks as 'top-5 all-time' and recordsInReach as 'per all-time record, the reigning holder'; _ordinal_label emits the literal string '<n>th-<thing> all-time' into the UI.
findings.observed: snapshot.build_public_snapshot walks the Sleeper previous_league_id chain capped at PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS (default 3). The chain currently terminates on its own — GET /v1/league/1090320428817592320 returns previous_league_id '0' for the 2024 season — so the 3-season window happens to equal the league's entire life and 'all-time' is true by accident. Nothing detects that coincidence. When the 2027 league is created the walk will stop at 2027/2026/2025 and drop 2024 entirely, at which point every string containing 'all-time' becomes false and no code, label or test will notice. Neither the payload nor the UI carries a windowIsCompleteHistory flag, and seasonsCovered is the only signal — which the record cards do not render.

priorFinding.note: The prior finding flags that docs/public_league.md states the wrong window size. This is the different and larger consequence: the cap silently invalidates the 'all-time' vocabulary, with zero headroom left.

findings.title: The gameplan recommendation objects state benefit and confidence but never cost; risk is reported only at position level and horizon only via a field the payload itself marks non-sortable
findings.claimUnderTest: Prompt: do recommendations state benefit, cost, risk, confidence and horizon?
findings.observed: Per-player targets carry BENEFIT (lineupGain, an exact re-solve delta — Travis Etienne +16.11), CONFIDENCE (0.5, and 0.85/0.0 at position level), and a reason plus a named corroborating-signal list. They carry NO COST — the payload states this explicitly in limitations.targets.cannotSupport: 'Any claim about what a trade will COST. The engines rank what is worth wanting, not what it takes to get it.' marketEdge is null on all 74 candidates because market_prices is deliberately omitted (coverage.marketEdgeUnmeasured explains that no validated conversion exists between the 0-100 rosValue index and the 0-9999 dynasty market). RISK appears only as positional concentrationRisk, never per recommendation. HORIZON appears only as targetPositions[].winNowWeight, which fieldPolicy.nonSortable and nonFilterable both disqualify because it carries two different quantities depending on viability. findings.userImpact: Zero today (no UI). Recorded because the gap is structural, not a bug: without an acquisition-cost scale the engine can rank what is worth wanting but cannot rank what is worth paying for, and any UI built on it would present a benefit with no price.
findings.whatWorks: This is the most honest omission set in the codebase. Every missing quantity is named, explained, and given a 'whatWouldUnlockMore' entry; the corroboration gate refuses to recommend on our own valuation alone (6 of 74 recommended, and coverage.corroborationYield explains that a yield near 100% would mean a corroborator had been fabricated); acceptancePlausibility carries a neverRenamed policy forbidding the word probability.
findings.rootCause: No acquisition-cost scale exists in the platform, and rosValue (0-100 index) and canonicalSiteValues (0-9999 market) have no validated conversion.

findings.title: A live headline about a CONTRACT extension multiplies Bijan Robinson's dynasty value by 0.9616 — src/api/injury_impact.py is a direct news-to-value multiplier with no structured claim, corroboration or module input
findings.claimUnderTest: The user's cardinal rule: news must never directly multiply a player value. It must flow source text -> structured claim -> source quality -> recency -> corroboration -> confidence-weighted assumption -> a MODULE INPUT -> value.
findings.observed: apply_injury_impact() goes headline -> keyword severity -> base% x position mult x age mult x linear decay -> adjustedValue = rankDerivedValue * adjustedPct/100. There is no structured claim (only the 3-bucket severity from a title regex), no source-quality term (a Sleeper drop-count row and a wire report are the same input), no corroboration requirement (ONE item is enough — the loop picks the worst-case single item), no confidence field, and no module input. The number is written to injuryAdjustedValue and rendered by InjuryChip on /terminal signal cards and inside PlayerPopup.

priorFinding.note: A12-F11 found the same module and correctly noted the 60%-vs-5% docstring mismatch and the Feb-Aug suppression. It framed the defect as documentation. The architectural violation — that this is a direct news-to-value multiplier at all, which is the user's single stated prohibition — is not in the prior registry, and the live-item numeric proof (a contract story discounting the player it is about) is new.

findings.whatWorks: The 5% cap, the 30-day linear decay and the Feb-Aug offseason suppressor all execute as written, and offseasonSuppressed is stamped on the result.
findings.rootCause: The module was designed as a 'lookup-table model' translating a news payload straight into a percentage on rankDerivedValue. Its only claim extraction is src/news/providers/_rss.py::classify(), a two-regex word-boundary match over title+description that returns one (severity, kind, impact) triple per ARTICLE.
findings.requiredRepair: Either (a) delete injuryAdjustedValue and let news drive labels only, or (b) route it the way BDVM already routes news: classify to a typed event, attach confidence + source reliability, require corroboration across providers, and feed a MODULE input (games, sigma, durability) rather than the final value. The BDVM path in src/bdvm/news_events.py is the working reference — see W21-F002.

findings.whatWorks: The >3-mention list-article cut, the ambiguous-mention skip, the closed ontology, the dedup-by-eventId and the 90-day auto-prune all behave as documented.
findings.rootCause: Claim extraction is a regex over the concatenation of headline and body, and attribution is 'every contract name found by substring anywhere in that text'. Neither step models which player the sentence containing the keyword is about.

findings.title: Structured events carry 6 of the 11 fields the event contract requires: no team, no source identity, no published-vs-effective split, no expected target, no duration, no review status
findings.claimUnderTest: An event should carry: type, player/team, source, reliability, published + effective timestamps, expected target, confidence, duration, decay/half-life, whether projections already reflect it, and review status.
findings.observed: PlayerEvent has event_id, player_key, event_type, effective_date, confidence, source_reliability, already_in_projection, impact, half_life_days, notes. Present: type, player, reliability (as a bare scalar), effective timestamp, confidence, half-life, already_in_projection. Absent: TEAM (nothing carries it, so a coordinator change or a depth-chart event cannot be scoped to a club); SOURCE identity (only the 0.6 scalar — which provider, which URL, which reporter is unrecoverable; news_events puts the headline in free-text notes and the item id inside the eventId string); PUBLISHED timestamp distinct from effective (both collapse to ts[:10], so a Monday report of a Saturday injury decays from the wrong date); EXPECTED TARGET (the impact dict names channels, not the quantity the event is predicted to move); DURATION (half-life is a decay rate, not an end date — a 4-game suspension is expressed as games_delta -4.0 with a 180-day half-life, so it fades rather than ending); REVIEW STATUS (there is no field — machine-vs-human is INFERRED by _is_auto() from an eventId string prefix plus confidence < 0.5, so a human confirming an auto event has no way to record 'reviewed' without also raising confidence, and a human-authored speculative event is indistinguishable from an unreviewed machine one).

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && .venv/bin/python -c "import dataclasses;from src.bdvm.events import PlayerEvent;print([f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(PlayerEvent)])" && .venv/bin/python -c "import json;print(sorted({k for v in json.load(open('config/bdvm/event_types_v1.json'))['event_types'].values() for k in v}))"
reproduction.expected: 11 required concepts representable
reproduction.actual: ['event_id','player_key','event_type','effective_date','confidence','source_reliability','already_in_projection','impact','half_life_days','notes']; ontology keys ['_comment','half_life_days','impact']

numericProof.formula: coverage = representable / required

findings.userImpact: Operationally: an operator auditing why a player's sigma widened sees a truncated headline in `notes` and cannot get back to the article, the reporter or the publish date. The review-status gap is the sharpest — _is_auto()'s own docstring concedes that raising confidence is the only way to mark human ownership, which conflates 'I checked this' with 'I believe it more', two different assertions.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior registry; A15-F11 audits the rules, not the record shape.

findings.whatWorks: Confidence, source_reliability, already_in_projection and half_life_days are all present, all load-bearing in decay_scale, and all honoured. The closed ontology with per-type half-lives is the right skeleton.
findings.rootCause: The schema was designed around what decay_scale needs to compute, not around what an auditor needs to reconstruct a claim.
findings.requiredRepair: Add team, sourceId/sourceUrl, publishedAt (distinct from effectiveDate), expiresAt, and reviewStatus ('auto'|'reviewed'|'authored') as first-class fields; derive _is_auto from reviewStatus instead of from an eventId prefix.

priorFinding.note: A10-F15 lists eleven zero-importer modules including src/news/unified_signal_engine.py. It does not include opportunity_stats.py or reception_shape_projection.py, and it does not connect the set to the usage/role capability claim or to the flag registry's own blind spot (a module with no flag entry cannot be caught by the reachability test that the registry advertises as its guarantee).

findings.title: `_sanitize_next_path` does not reject a backslash, so `/login?next=/\evil.com` is a working post-authentication open redirect on the real domain
findings.claimUnderTest: frontend/middleware.js:52-54 — "server.py::_sanitize_next_path rejects absolute URLs and CR/LF on the way back out." The guard is presented as the complete sanitiser for the post-login destination.
findings.observed: The guard rejects `http://`, `https://`, a leading `//`, a non-`/` prefix and CR/LF — but not a backslash. `next=/\evil.com` survives verbatim and is returned as `{"ok":true,"redirect":"/\\evil.com"}`. `frontend/app/login/page.jsx:25` re-checks only `next.startsWith("/")`, which `/\evil.com` satisfies, then line 50 calls `router.push(data.redirect)`. Next resolves the href with the WHATWG URL parser, which normalises `\` to `/` for special schemes, so `new URL('/\\evil.com', location.href)` is `http://evil.com/`. Driven end to end in Chromium against the real login form, the browser issued a top-level navigation to `http://evil.com/` immediately after a successful login. `/\/evil.com` passes too.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W22/open-redirect-repro.py   # needs a backend on :8001 with ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1; header-only check: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"x","password":"y","next":"/\\evil.com"}'
reproduction.expected: redirect coerced to "/" exactly as it is for `//evil.com` and `https://evil.com`
reproduction.actual: redirect = "/\\evil.com"; Chromium then requests http://evil.com/ — captured as offsite requests: ['http://evil.com/']

numericProof.formula: offsite := new URL(next, origin).origin !== origin

findings.userImpact: A link on the genuine chaseupside.com domain — `https://chaseupside.com/login?next=/\attacker.tld` — shows the real login page, takes the operator's real password, and then drops the browser on the attacker's site. That is the standard credential-phishing amplifier: the victim has no domain cue that anything is wrong, and the attacker's landing page can render a convincing "session expired, sign in again" form. With a single shared operator credential (W22-F003) and no MFA, one success is full compromise.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding in the 531-item index mentions open redirect or _sanitize_next_path.

findings.whatWorks: The three cases the guard was written for — `//host`, `http(s)://host`, and CR/LF header injection — are all correctly coerced to "/". The frontend's own `startsWith("/")` check is a second layer and also correct as far as it goes.
findings.rootCause: A denylist of four dangerous prefixes instead of an allowlist. The set of strings a browser treats as scheme-relative is larger than `//`: RFC 3986 says backslash is not a path separator, but the WHATWG URL Standard (which every browser and Next's router use) maps `\` to `/` inside special-scheme URLs.
findings.requiredRepair: Replace the prefix denylist with a parse-and-compare: `u = urlsplit(value)`; reject unless `u.scheme == '' and u.netloc == '' and value.startswith('/')`, after normalising backslashes to forward slashes first. Add `/\\evil.com`, `/\/evil.com`, `/%5Cevil.com` and `/\t/evil.com` to whatever test pins this.
findings.dependencies: None. Self-contained one-function fix in server.py.

findings.title: The rate limiter keys on an unvalidated client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For`, so every public endpoint's limit is bypassed by rotating one header
findings.claimUnderTest: src/api/rate_limit.py:9-11 — "60 requests/minute per IP … 1000 requests/hour per IP (burst cap)", and server.py:2840-2842 "Also applies rate limiting to public endpoints … to protect against scraper abuse."
findings.observed: `_client_ip_from_request` returns the FIRST comma-separated entry of `X-Forwarded-For` whenever the header is present, with no trusted-proxy check and no fallback preference for `request.client.host`. nginx sets `X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`, which APPENDS `$remote_addr` to whatever the client sent — so in production the first entry is entirely attacker-controlled. Measured on a second backend booted without `RATE_LIMIT_BYPASS_IPS`: the real client IP was driven to a hard 429, and 20 consecutive requests sent from that same socket with rotating `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.N` all returned 200.

reproduction.command:
# boot a backend on :8001 without RATE_LIMIT_BYPASS_IPS, then:
for i in $(seq 1 70); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/health; done
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/health   # 429
for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%s ' -H "X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.$i" http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/health; done
reproduction.expected: 429 for all 20, because they originate from the throttled socket

numericProof.formula: 429_count over 20 spoofed-XFF requests issued from an already-throttled socket

findings.userImpact: The scraper-abuse defence the module exists for does not exist. Anyone can pull the 2.08 MB `/api/public/league` contract, or the 47 KB `/api/news` feed, at whatever rate the box will serve — and, because `/api/auth/login` sits behind the same limiter, the login endpoint has no effective throttle either (W22-F003).

priorFinding.note: No prior finding mentions X-Forwarded-For or the rate limiter.

findings.whatWorks: The token-bucket arithmetic itself is correct and thread-safe: 60 requests pass and the 61st gets 429 with a sane `Retry-After`, refill is proportional to elapsed time, and the `_MAX_TRACKED_IPS` eviction bounds memory. The limiter fails open around a raising `should_rate_limit`, which is the right posture. Nothing here is wrong except the key.
findings.rootCause: `_client_ip_from_request` trusts a hop-by-hop header unconditionally. The comment "First entry in the chain is the original client" is true only when every hop appends and the leftmost hop is itself trusted — which is exactly what `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for` does NOT guarantee for a directly-reachable client.
findings.requiredRepair: Prefer `X-Real-IP` (nginx sets it from `$remote_addr` and OVERWRITES, so it is not client-controlled) and fall back to `request.client.host`; use `X-Forwarded-For` only after stripping a configured count of trusted proxy hops from the RIGHT. `_MAX_TRACKED_IPS`-based eviction also becomes a memory-exhaustion lever while the key is attacker-chosen.
findings.dependencies: nginx already sets `X-Real-IP $remote_addr` in both `location /api/` and `location /`, so no deploy change is needed.

findings.title: Login has no throttle of its own, no lockout and no failure backoff — 200 wrong-password attempts landed at 223 req/s with zero 429
findings.claimUnderTest: HANDOFF.md's known-issues list states there is NO login rate limiting. The code's own position is the opposite: `/api/auth/login` is in `_PUBLIC_API_EXACT`, so the 60/min public-endpoint limiter does cover it.
findings.observed: Both are half right, and the net effect is HANDOFF.md's. The generic limiter is the ONLY throttle: `auth_login` itself has no attempt counter, no per-account lockout, no backoff, and no delay. That limiter is (a) shared with every other public endpoint — 60 requests to `/api/public/league` in the same minute leave the operator locked out of their own login — and (b) keyed on a spoofable header (W22-F002). Measured on a limiter-live backend: 120 wrong-password POSTs from one IP → {401: 18, 429: 102}; the same 200 POSTs with a rotating `X-Forwarded-For` → {401: 200} in 0.9 s, zero 429. There is exactly ONE credential (`JASON_LOGIN_USERNAME`/`JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD`) and no second factor. Guest-pass tokens are 24 random URL-safe bytes and are not brute-forceable, but the operator password is whatever a human chose.

reproduction.command:
# on a backend booted WITHOUT RATE_LIMIT_BYPASS_IPS:
.venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import json,time,urllib.request,urllib.error
c={}
t=time.time()
for i in range(200):
    b=json.dumps({"username":"jasonleetucker","password":f"wrong-{i}"}).encode()
    r=urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/auth/login",data=b,headers={"Content-Type":"application/json","X-Forwarded-For":f"198.51.100.{i%250}"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(r,timeout=10) as x: s=x.status
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: s=e.code
    c[s]=c.get(s,0)+1
print(c, time.time()-t)
EOF
reproduction.expected: a lockout or exponential backoff after a handful of failures for the same username
reproduction.actual: {401: 200} in 0.9 s = 223 attempts/second, no 429, no delay, no lockout

numericProof.formula: attempts/sec = attempts / elapsed; 401-only means every attempt was evaluated

findings.userImpact: An 8-character lowercase-alphanumeric operator password is ~2.8e12 candidates; at 223/s from one host that is not reachable, but the rate is bounded only by the attacker's willingness to run parallel sources, and nothing anywhere records or alerts on a burst of failures. More practically: a leaked or reused password gets confirmed instantly, and there is no signal in any log, on `/api/status`, or in the alert path that a credential-stuffing run happened at all.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A10-F08 cites 'the login rate-limit gap' as one of the HANDOFF.md items that IS still true. Confirmed in substance and refined: a generic limiter does cover the route, it is simply shared and bypassable, and the missing pieces are the login-specific ones (lockout, backoff, failure telemetry).

findings.whatWorks: `hmac.compare_digest` is used for the two cron bearer tokens. Guest-pass validation is a hashed-token table lookup, so it is constant-time by construction and the plaintext is never stored. The cookie is HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax with a 30-day max-age matching the server-side TTL, session ids are `uuid.uuid4().hex` (122 bits from os.urandom), and guest sessions carry a server-side `expires_at_epoch` re-checked on every request so a stretched cookie cannot outlive its pass.
findings.rootCause: Login was treated as just another public endpoint. Nothing distinguishes 'one anonymous read of a public board' from 'one attempt at the only credential that exists'.
findings.requiredRepair: Add a per-username failure counter with exponential backoff (and a hard lockout window), keyed independently of IP so header spoofing cannot reset it; emit a log line and an alert on N failures; and fix the limiter key (W22-F002) so the IP-side throttle is real. `password == JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD` at server.py:9838 should also become `hmac.compare_digest` for consistency with the bearer paths.
findings.dependencies: W22-F002 — the IP-side half is worthless until the key is trustworthy.

findings.title: `ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1` silently makes `changeme` a full admin password, has no production guard, and is invisible on every health/status surface
findings.claimUnderTest: tests/conftest.py:11 — "production rejects ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1 by design." server.py:174-176 — "this guard prevents a misconfigured restart from silently shipping a known password."
findings.observed: Neither is true. There is no production check of any kind: the branch is `if not password: if _env_bool('ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV', False): password = 'changeme'`. Nothing consults an environment name, a hostname, `JASON_AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE`, or anything else. The only signal is one WARNING at import time, which scrolls out of `journalctl` and appears nowhere at runtime — `startup_validation.run_all()` checks eight things and none of them is the login password or this flag, so `/api/health.startupChecks` reports `total: 8, ok: 8, failed: 0` on a box running the placeholder password. Proven live: on a backend with `ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1` and `JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD` unset, `jasonleetucker`/`changeme` returned 200, `/api/auth/status` reported `isAdmin: true`, and `GET /api/admin/guest-passes` returned 200. The second failure mode is separate and not guarded at all: `.env.example` ships `JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD=changeme`, so an operator who copies it to `.env` gets the same outcome with the flag OFF, because the import-time guard fires only on UNSET, never on weak.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && env -u JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1 .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');import server;from fastapi.testclient import TestClient;c=TestClient(server.app);print(c.post('/api/auth/login',json={'username':'jasonleetucker','password':'changeme'}).status_code);print(c.get('/api/auth/status').json())"
reproduction.expected: either a refusal to boot in a production-shaped environment, or at minimum a visible degraded marker on /api/health and /api/status
reproduction.actual: 200 + {"authenticated":true,"username":"jasonleetucker","isAdmin":true}; /api/health startupChecks says total 8 / ok 8 / failed 0

numericProof.formula: count of startup_validation checks whose name matches JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD|ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV

findings.userImpact: One stray line in `.env` — or one `.env.example` copied verbatim — hands full admin over `chaseupside.com` to anyone who guesses a five-year-old default, and the operator has no way to notice: the app looks healthy on every surface they can check. Combined with the unbounded login rate (W22-F003), detection time is the only thing standing between the misconfiguration and compromise.

priorFinding.note: The April 2026 report (audit/AUDIT_REPORT_2026-04-28.md C1) closed the hardcoded-default incident; nothing in the 531-item prior index re-examines the escape hatch it introduced.

findings.whatWorks: The import-time RuntimeError for the fully-unset case is real and correct — `EnvironmentFile=-.../.env` means a missing .env produces a crash loop rather than a silent weak-password boot, which is the right failure. The password is genuinely out of source: 0 tracked files carry a literal, and the three docs that quoted the old one now carry `«REDACTED — see audit/AUDIT_REPORT_2026-04-28.md C1»`.
findings.rootCause: A dev escape hatch with no environment discriminator, plus a startup validator that checks directories and SQLite files but no security-relevant configuration.
findings.requiredRepair: (1) Gate the flag on an explicit non-production marker (e.g. refuse when `JASON_AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE` is true, or require an `APP_ENV=dev`). (2) Add two `startup_validation` checks — `env:JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD` required, and a `fatal=False` check that fails when the effective password equals the placeholder — so the condition is visible on `/api/health`. (3) Change `.env.example` to `JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD=` (empty) so a verbatim copy crash-loops instead of booting weak. (4) Fix the false comment at tests/conftest.py:11.
findings.dependencies: Note that adding the check to startup_validation puts it on TWO anonymous endpoints — see W22-F005; emit the check name only, never the value.

findings.title: `/api/status`, `/api/health` and `/api/scaffold/status` hand absolute deploy paths, env-var presence, feature-flag state, the full source inventory and live session counts to anonymous callers
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md's endpoint table for `/api/leagues`: "stable `key` → `displayName` + roster settings; **no Sleeper IDs leaked**", and the routing section's "no endpoint exposes raw Sleeper IDs to the UI".
findings.observed: `/api/leagues` honours the invariant exactly — 808 bytes, zero Sleeper ids. `/api/status`, on the same public allowlist and with no comment justifying its presence there, emits `leagues[].sleeperLeagueId` for BOTH registry leagues. It also emits, anonymously: absolute deploy paths (`/home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/data/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json`, `.../data/rank_history.jsonl`), the complete `featureFlags` map with `gateStatus`, `served_source_coverage` naming all 21 ranking sources with per-source row counts, `source_health.source_failures` with free-text failure reasons, `run_events`, and payload byte sizes. `/api/health` adds the `startupChecks` array — three absolute directory paths, two SQLite filenames, the league-registry keys, and `env:PRIVATE_APP_ALLOWED_USERNAMES → "missing (optional)"`, which tells a stranger the allowlist env var is unset and therefore that the admin username is the in-code default `jasonleetucker` — plus `session_cookies` naming the three paid subscription session files, per-breaker `lastError` strings, `memberInMemorySessions: 42`, `sessions.persistedCount`, and `backup_health.newestBackupPath`. `/api/scaffold/status` adds two more absolute paths and identity-pipeline counts.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/status | grep -o '"sleeperLeagueId": "[0-9]*"'; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health | grep -o 'env:PRIVATE_APP_ALLOWED_USERNAMES.\{0,60\}'; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/scaffold/status | grep -o '/home/[^"]*'; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/leagues | grep -c sleeperLeagueId
reproduction.expected: the /api/leagues invariant applied consistently across the public allowlist; no absolute paths, no env-var inventory, no operator counts
reproduction.actual: /api/status: 2 sleeperLeagueId values + 2 absolute paths + 15 feature flags + 21 source names; /api/health: env:PRIVATE_APP_ALLOWED_USERNAMES 'missing (optional)' + 3 absolute dirs + 3 vendor session filenames + 42 in-memory sessions; /api/scaffold/status: 2 absolute paths; /api/leagues: 0

numericProof.formula: count of _PUBLIC_API_EXACT routes emitting host filesystem paths or registry Sleeper ids

findings.userImpact: An attacker profiling the deployment gets the app root, the data directory layout, which SQLite files exist, which env vars are unset (so which defaults are live — including the admin username), which feature flags are on, the entire scraping source list with coverage, and the live session count, without authenticating. None of it is exploitable on its own; all of it shortens the reconnaissance step for everything else in this shard. The `/api/leagues` redaction is undone in substance by a sibling on the same allowlist, so the documented invariant does not describe the system.

priorFinding.note: CONFIRMED for the mechanism and both named routes, refuted on the stated impact of the id leak. PRIOR-A23-F16 says the ids enable 'direct enumeration of rosters, transactions and drafts via Sleeper's open API'. That is true, but the incremental exposure is ZERO: config/leagues/registry.json is a TRACKED file in a PUBLIC repository carrying both ids, and SECURITY.md explicitly accepts that ('the league configuration … readable by anyone'). I verified the ids do unlock the second league via api.sleeper.app. The real defect is that the invariant CLAUDE.md documents is applied to one public route and not another — a doc/code contradiction, not a data leak. The absolute-path half is confirmed unqualified, and I add the env-var-inventory, feature-flag, source-inventory, vendor-session-filename and session-count disclosures the prior finding did not cover.

findings.whatWorks: `/api/leagues` genuinely withholds every Sleeper id while still serving the roster settings the frontend needs, and `/api/metrics` and `/api/uptime` carry nothing sensitive. The global exception handler never returns a traceback — it emits `errorType` only and logs the trace server-side — and 13 anonymous probes with traversal, null-byte, negative and overflow inputs produced zero raw exception text.
findings.rootCause: `_PUBLIC_API_EXACT` was assembled per-consumer ('the /league page needs this') without a payload review. Every other public route in the set carries an explaining comment; `/api/status`, `/api/health`, `/api/metrics` and `/api/scaffold/status` carry none.
findings.requiredRepair: Either move `/api/status` and `/api/scaffold/status` behind the session gate (the only in-tree consumer of `/api/status` is `/admin`, which is already a private page — this is what makes PRIOR-A06-F08 possible) or give them an anonymous projection: drop `leagues[].sleeperLeagueId`, replace absolute paths with basenames, drop `startupChecks` env rows and `run_events`, and keep the full payload for authenticated callers.
findings.dependencies: `/admin` currently relies on `/api/status` being public for its load-time fetch (W22-F008); gating it is the fix for both.

findings.title: `sitemap.js` is an unwired fourth consumer of the public/private page split and advertises the private `/trades`; `robots.js` still allows the `/league/insider-trading` exception it was supposed to close
findings.claimUnderTest: public-routes.js:5-8 — "One predicate, three consumers: middleware.js, AppShellWrapper.jsx, robots.js … It lives here, pure and dependency-free, because those three used to disagree." And :44-62 — the `/league/insider-trading` exception, added because "`robots.txt` serves `Allow: /league/`, so that spinner is on an indexable URL."
findings.observed: There are FOUR consumers. `frontend/app/sitemap.js` imports nothing from `public-routes.js` and hardcodes its own "Static public routes" list containing `"/trades"` — the one route whose privacy the module's own header comment spends a paragraph explaining. The live `sitemap.xml` therefore publishes `https://chaseupside.com/trades` while middleware 307s that exact path to `/login` and `robots.txt` disallows it. Separately, the `/league/insider-trading` fix was applied to `isPublicPath` only: `robots.js` spreads `PUBLIC_PREFIXES` and ignores `PRIVATE_EXCEPTIONS`, so the emitted `robots.txt` is `Allow: /league/` + `Disallow: /` with no `Disallow: /league/insider-trading`. Under longest-match precedence that URL remains crawlable-by-policy — which is the precise condition the comment says the exception was written to end. (`robots.js` also omits `PUBLIC_EXACT`, so the legitimately-public `/draft-capital` shim is disallowed.)

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/sitemap.xml | grep -o '<loc>[^<]*trades</loc>'; curl -s -o /dev/null -D- http://127.0.0.1:3000/trades | grep -i '^location'; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/robots.txt; grep -n 'public-routes' frontend/app/sitemap.js || echo 'sitemap.js: NO IMPORT'
reproduction.expected: every sitemap entry satisfies isPublicPath(); robots.txt disallows every PRIVATE_EXCEPTIONS path
reproduction.actual: <loc>https://chaseupside.com/trades</loc> while /trades → 307 /login?next=%2Ftrades; robots.txt has Allow: /league/ and no insider-trading Disallow; sitemap.js: NO IMPORT

numericProof.formula: count of sitemap <loc> paths for which isPublicPath(path) === false

findings.userImpact: No data leaks — every private page still 307s and robots.txt still disallows `/trades`. What breaks is the guarantee: the module that exists to stop these three files disagreeing is not consulted by the fourth, so the next private page added to `sitemap.js`'s static list, or the next `/league/*` page added anywhere, repeats the `/league/insider-trading` incident with nothing to catch it. A crawler that reads the sitemap and ignores robots gets a permanent 307 loop on an advertised URL.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers sitemap.js or robots.js consistency.

findings.whatWorks: The gate itself is airtight in both directions: all 18 private pages probed anonymously returned 307 to `/login?next=<encoded original>`, the four public ones returned 200, `/draft-capital` returned a real 308 to its new home, and neither anonymous 200's HTML contained any private-board token. `robots.js` correctly rebuilt itself as an allowlist, and `middleware.js` is genuinely the single page-auth gate now that server.py registers no page routes (confirmed: `curl :8000/rankings` → JSON 404).
findings.rootCause: `sitemap.js` predates or was written alongside `public-routes.js` and was never migrated; `robots.js` was migrated to `PUBLIC_PREFIXES` before `PRIVATE_EXCEPTIONS` existed and was not revisited when the exception landed.
findings.requiredRepair: Import `isPublicPath` in `sitemap.js` and filter every entry through it (fails closed for future pages); spread `PUBLIC_EXACT` into `robots.js`'s allow list and `PRIVATE_EXCEPTIONS` into a `disallow` array; add a test that asserts every sitemap entry satisfies `isPublicPath` and every `PRIVATE_EXCEPTIONS` entry appears in robots' disallow.

findings.title: Operator-grade actions and pages are gated on session PRESENCE, not on the admin allowlist, so a guest-pass holder can trigger a production scrape, an email send and an intel crawl
findings.claimUnderTest: server.py:9856-9859 — a guest-pass session's username is left as the literal `"guest"` so "downstream admin gates … reject guests automatically — a guest can browse the private surface but cannot trigger admin actions or generate more passes." And frontend/app/admin/page.jsx:7-9 — "Access is gated server-side by PRIVATE_APP_ALLOWED_USERNAMES."
findings.observed: True only for the six routes under `/api/admin/*`, all of which I confirmed return 403 `admin_required` to a non-admin session. The operator-grade actions that live OUTSIDE that prefix have no allowlist check at all — the session-presence middleware is their entire authorization. `POST /api/scrape` (`async def trigger_scrape`) never calls `_require_admin_session`; `POST /api/test-alert` is declared `async def test_alert()` with no `Request` parameter, so it cannot check anything; `POST /api/intel/refresh` accepts any session (`if not is_cron and not session: 401`) and applies only a per-user cooldown. Page-side, `middleware.js` checks cookie PRESENCE only, so `/admin` and all three `/tools/*` returned 200 to the non-admin `e2e-test-user` session, and `/admin`'s sole load-time fetch is `/api/status` — a PUBLIC route — so its "Not authorized" branch is unreachable. Separately, every guest-pass session is created with username `"guest"` while `user_kv.user_state` has `username TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, so all guests share one row: watchlist, `activeLeagueKey`, `selectedTeam`, `siteWeights`, dismissed signals and `customAlerts` are overwritten guest-by-guest, and a guest's `customAlerts` rules are executed by the daily sweep.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat .../e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"; for p in /admin /tools/source-health /tools/ros-data-health /tools/trade-coverage; do curl -s -b /tmp/c -o /dev/null -w "$p %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:3000$p; done; grep -n 'async def trigger_scrape' -A3 server.py; grep -n 'async def test_alert' -A2 server.py
reproduction.expected: 403 admin_required for operator-grade actions and pages, matching the /api/admin/* posture the docstrings describe
reproduction.actual: /admin 200, /tools/source-health 200, /tools/ros-data-health 200, /tools/trade-coverage 200; trigger_scrape and test_alert contain no admin check (test_alert takes no Request at all)

numericProof.formula: count of operator-grade handlers outside /api/admin/* that call _require_admin_session

findings.userImpact: Anyone the operator hands a guest pass to — the stated purpose is showing the tool to leaguemates — can start a full production scrape (minutes of Playwright work plus outbound traffic to every ranking site), fire the configured email alert, kick off the multi-minute budgeted Sleeper intel crawl, and read the operator dashboard including live feature-flag state and scrape internals. They can also silently overwrite every other guest's saved settings and plant alert rules that the nightly sweep will run. None of it is destructive to player data, but none of it is what the docstring promises either.

priorFinding.note: CONFIRMED at runtime — /admin returns 200 to a non-admin session and its only mount-time fetch is the public /api/status, exactly as described. Extended on three axes the prior finding did not cover: the three /tools/* pages behave identically, three operator-grade API routes outside /api/admin/* have no allowlist check at all, and every guest-pass session collides on the single user_kv row keyed 'guest'.

findings.whatWorks: `_require_admin_session` is correct and is the first statement of all six `/api/admin/*` handlers — five verified live returning 403 to a non-admin session and 401 anonymously. Guest passes are well built: 24-byte `secrets.token_urlsafe` tokens, SHA-256 at rest with the plaintext shown once, a 30-day creation cap, revocation, opportunistic purge, and a server-side `expires_at_epoch` re-checked on every request so a stretched cookie cannot outlive the pass. The two cron bearer routes fail closed — they short-circuit before touching cookies when the token is unset, use `hmac.compare_digest`, and require `auth_method == "password"` on the session fallback, which excludes guest and e2e sessions.
findings.rootCause: Two authorization tiers exist (session, allowlist) but only the `/api/admin/*` prefix was wired to the second one. Route placement, not route capability, decided which tier applied.
findings.requiredRepair: Add `_require_admin_session` to `trigger_scrape`, `test_alert` (which needs a `Request` parameter first) and `post_intel_refresh`'s non-cron branch; give `middleware.js` an admin-page list checked against a lightweight allowlist claim, or have `/admin` and `/tools/*` fetch a genuinely admin-gated endpoint on mount so the existing "Not authorized" branch can fire; and namespace guest user_kv rows per pass id (`guest:{guest_pass_id}`) instead of the shared literal.
findings.dependencies: The `/admin` page fix is coupled to W22-F005 — gating `/api/status` makes the page's existing 403 branch work with no page change.

findings.title: The public-league payload's name-based blocklist cannot see derived values: 393 anonymous trade grades encode bracketed value ratios computed from `rankDerivedValue`
findings.claimUnderTest: src/api/public_activity_valuation.py:1-12 — "The public src/public_league package is strictly isolated from private rankings … The raw values that drive the grade never leave the backend — only the derived grade block appears on the public payload." SECURITY.md — "player valuations, trade tooling, waiver and draft analysis, and BDVM output are all login-gated."
findings.observed: The literal claim holds: `assert_public_payload_safe` walks every dict key at every depth against a 39-name blocklist and I confirmed 0 hits for any blocklisted field across ten anonymous public endpoints totalling 2.6 MB. But the guard is a NAME blocklist, so it is structurally blind to a value derived from a blocked field and stored under an unblocked name. `/api/public/league` serves 191 graded trades / 393 graded sides anonymously. Each side carries its full received and sent asset lists AND a grade letter that is a five-band quantisation of `package_value(received)/package_value(sent)` at cut points 3/8/15/25/40 percent, where the values come from the private contract's `displayValue`/`rankDerivedValue`. That is 393 published inequality constraints over a few hundred distinct assets — a solvable system for relative board values to within-band precision, obtainable with no session.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys,collections;d=json.load(sys.stdin);f=d['sections']['activity']['feed'];g=[s for t in f for s in (t.get('sides') or []) if isinstance(s,dict) and s.get('grade')];print(len(f),'trades',len(g),'graded sides');print(collections.Counter(s['grade']['grade'] for s in g))"
reproduction.expected: per the isolation docstring, nothing on the anonymous payload that is a function of rankDerivedValue
reproduction.actual: 191 trades / 393 graded sides; Counter({'A+': 114, 'F': 60, 'A': 55, 'D': 53, 'B+': 41, 'B': 25, 'A-': 23, 'C': 22}), each paired with the exact asset list on both sides

numericProof.formula: published constraints = graded sides; each is log2(5) ≈ 2.32 bits about package_value(received)/package_value(sent)

findings.userImpact: A competitor who wants the board does not need to break the auth gate; they need to fit 393 published ratio brackets. The recovered board would be coarse — bands, not values — but ordering and rough magnitude are exactly what the tool sells. Second-order: every manager's per-trade verdict from the operator's private model is public and attributed by `ownerId` and `displayName`, which is league-social information the operator may not have intended to publish.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding examines the derived-value channel through the public contract guard.

findings.whatWorks: The isolation architecture is real and does the hard part correctly: `src/public_league` never imports the contract, `server.py` injects a callable, and the raw numbers genuinely never appear — verified byte-level across ten endpoints. The `/api/draft-capital` redaction is the same problem solved properly: `_redact_draft_capital_for_public` strips all five rookie-board fields from 72/72 picks for anonymous callers, stamps `rookieBoardRedacted: true`, and does it on a COPY so the shared TTL cache is not poisoned for the authenticated /draft page. That is the pattern the grade channel needs.
findings.rootCause: `assert_public_payload_safe` was designed against accidental field passthrough (a rename, a new bundle key) and is well suited to that. Deliberate derivation is a different threat and the guard has no way to express it, because the derived output is legitimately named `grade`.
findings.requiredRepair: This is a product decision, not a bug fix, and it should be recorded as one rather than left implicit in a docstring that reads as an absolute. If the grades stay: state in the isolation docstring and in SECURITY.md that a bounded derived signal is deliberately published, and consider widening the bands or dropping the letter to a three-way win/fair/loss to cut the recoverable precision. If they should not be public: pass `activity_valuation=None` on the anonymous path and keep grades for authenticated callers only, mirroring `_redact_draft_capital_for_public`.
findings.dependencies: None technically; needs an owner decision on intent.

findings.title: `/api/draft-capital` serves auth-varying bodies under `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60` with no `Vary: Cookie`, and `/api/auth/status` sends no cache directive at all
findings.claimUnderTest: deploy/nginx/chaseupside-proxy.conf:88-95 — "tests/api/test_cache_control_privacy.py documents the invariant that auth-gated endpoints must not meet a shared cache … /api responses pass through uncached with their app-stamped private/no-store Cache-Control intact."
findings.observed: The shared-cache half of the invariant holds — nginx attaches `proxy_cache` only to `/_next/static/`, and `private` would bar a shared cache anyway. The per-browser half is unhandled. `/api/draft-capital` returns two different bodies for the same URL depending on the session cookie (the five rookie-board fields plus `rookieBoardRedacted`), yet stamps `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding` only. A browser that loaded the public `/league` draft-capital tab and then signed in serves the redacted body from its private cache for up to 60 s (300 s stale-while-revalidate), so `/draft` renders with no rookie names; the reverse holds after logout. `/api/auth/status` returns username, `authMethod` and `isAdmin` with NO `Cache-Control` header at all, so its freshness is left to browser heuristics — the only session-identity endpoint in the app without `no-store`, while `/api/user/state` and `/api/leagues` both set it.

reproduction.command: for u in /api/draft-capital /api/auth/status /api/user/state; do echo "-- $u"; curl -s -o /dev/null -D- -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000$u" | grep -iE '^(cache-control|vary):' | tr -d '\r'; done
reproduction.expected: draft-capital: Vary: Cookie alongside private (or no-store); auth-status: Cache-Control: no-store
reproduction.actual: draft-capital: 'cache-control: private, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300' + 'vary: Accept-Encoding' (no Cookie); auth-status: no cache-control header emitted at all

numericProof.formula: seconds a stale variant can be served after an auth transition = max-age + stale-while-revalidate

findings.userImpact: For up to six minutes after signing in on a browser that had just viewed the public league page, `/draft` shows a rookie board with every name, position and value blank and no explanation. Confined to one browser profile, so this is a correctness and confusion defect rather than a disclosure one. The missing `no-store` on `/api/auth/status` risks a stale identity — showing a signed-out shell to a signed-in user or vice versa — after a back-navigation.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers Vary on the redacted draft-capital response.

findings.whatWorks: The redaction itself is exemplary and I could not break it: full payload cached, redaction applied per-response on a copy, `rookieBoardRedacted` stamped so a client can tell redaction from absence. Every genuinely private route carries `private` or `no-store`; nginx caches only `/_next/static/`; and no `/api/*` response I saw set both `Set-Cookie` and a cacheable directive.
findings.rootCause: The response was designed as a single cacheable artifact and the redaction was added later as a per-response transform. The cache directive was not revisited to declare the new dimension of variance.
findings.requiredRepair: Add `Vary: Cookie` to both `JSONResponse` returns in `get_draft_capital` (or set `no-store` on the authenticated variant and keep `private, max-age=60` for the anonymous one, which is the cheaper option since the anonymous variant is what the high-traffic public page hits). Add `Cache-Control: no-store` to `auth_status`. Extend `tests/api/test_cache_control_privacy.py` to assert that any route whose body varies by session declares it.

findings.title: The audit's own skip census undercounts skip sites 6x (27 declared, 166 actual) because it greps only `pytest.skip(` and misses 139 unittest-style skip sites
findings.claimUnderTest: evidence/test-results-summary.txt says '## Static census of skip/xfail markers (skips are runtime, so this is the declared set)' and lists 27 lines, framing that as the complete declared skip surface behind a 6,278-pass green run.
findings.observed: The census regex matches only `pytest.skip(` and `pytest.mark.skipif`. The suite is majority-unittest, and 139 further skip sites use `self.skipTest(...)` / `unittest.skipIf(...)`, which the census cannot see. Total is 166 sites in 43 files. The three largest are invisible to the census entirely: tests/api/test_launch_readiness.py (26 sites), tests/api/test_single_curve_live.py (17), tests/api/test_draft_capital.py (17). A skipped test and a passing test are byte-identical in `pytest -q` output, and no workflow asserts a minimum collected/passed count, so the declared figure is what a reader uses to size the risk.

reproduction.expected: 27, matching the census in evidence/test-results-summary.txt
reproduction.actual: TOTAL skip sites: 166 in 43 files; top files test_launch_readiness.py=26, test_single_curve_live.py=17, test_draft_capital.py=17, test_source_monitoring.py=15, test_picks_end_to_end.py=12

numericProof.formula: actual = pytest_style + unittest_style

findings.userImpact: A maintainer reading the green run sizes the false-confidence surface at 27 self-skipping assertions and moves on. The real figure is 166, concentrated in exactly the modules that assert against the live board (launch readiness, the single-curve invariants, the draft-capital workbook). tests/api/test_draft_capital.py is NOT livedata-marked, so its 17 skip sites sit in the BLOCKING tier: if openpyxl or CSVs/Draft Data.xlsx goes missing, the only check that a Sleeper-traded pick moves auction dollars in the right direction evaporates into a green PR.

priorFinding.note: Prior counted 157 in 30 files at commit 9c5d972; I measure 166 in 43 files at e96c06ef with a superset regex (adds unittest.skipIf/skipUnless). The new half is that the MASTER AUDIT'S OWN evidence file re-introduced the undercount at 27.

findings.whatWorks: Every skip carries a human-readable reason string; none are bare. tests/consensus_edge/test_panel.py's 10 shallow-clone skips are correctly gated on an explicit `panel.is_shallow()` and do NOT fire in CI (pr-validation.yml:65 and deploy.yml:43 both set fetch-depth: 0).

findings.title: tests/consensus_edge/test_scoring.py:301 asserts a cached object's field against itself and cannot detect an unstable paramSetId
findings.claimUnderTest: `test_param_set_id_is_stable` — the name asserts that the content-hashed parameter-set identifier is reproducible across calls, which is what makes a payload's `paramSetId` a meaningful version stamp.
findings.observed: `self.assertEqual(params_mod.load()['paramSetId'], params_mod.load()['paramSetId'])`. `params.load()` memoizes into a module-level `_CACHE` (params.py:25) and returns it verbatim on any subsequent call with `path=None, refresh=False` (params.py:61-62). Both sides of the assertion are therefore the same dict object's same key — the equality is `x == x` on one object. A paramSetId derived from `id()`, a timestamp, or unstable dict ordering would pass this test unchanged, because the hash is computed exactly once.

If it stopped being content-derived, cached responses and stored verdicts would be compared under a stamp that no longer identifies anything, and the only test named for that property would stay green. Impact is bounded because the `consensus_edge` flag defaults off (ADR-023).

findings.title: The league-adjusted board's scarcity is measured entirely in ROS log-rank units, so a 0-100 ordinal index sets the multiplier on every dynasty trade value under the adjusted lens
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: the valuation overlay is driven by 'positional scarcity from this league's 12 rosters'. It does not say the scarcity is measured in ROS units.
findings.observed: compute_scarcity reads value = float(p.get('rosValue')) for every rostered player (replacement.py:631) out of data/ros/team_strength/<league>.json, and measure_endogenous_starters solves the lineup over the same field. lineupScarcity is a RATIO of two rosValues, so it is dimensionless and no scale is mixed - but rosValue is 100*(ln(N+1)-ln(r))/ln(N+1), an ordinal log-rank index (ros/aggregate.py:171, gameplan.py:40-49). A ratio of two ordinal indices is not a cardinal 'drop from the top player to the last starter'. That ratio becomes factor = 1 + (lineupScarcity - 0.5)*0.20 (adjustment.py:247) and multiplies every dynasty value the engines serve. Live: WR lineupScarcity 0.634 -> factor 1.0268; DL 0.767 -> 1.0978; LB 0.598 -> 0.9797. replacement.py:20-52 documents the known bias honestly (projection path measures FLEX-TE share at 0.0% vs 10.4% on weekly actuals) but the docstring lives on the measurement function, not on the published board.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w29.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/valuation/league-adjusted | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print({k:round(v['lineupScarcity'],4) for k,v in d['scarcity'].items()}); print({k:d['factors'][k] for k in list(d['factors'])[:4]})"
reproduction.expected: scarcity documented as derived from a cardinal value scale
reproduction.actual: lineupScarcity values 0.436-0.767 are ratios of rosValue, a 0-100 ordinal log-rank index; factors 0.953-1.043 multiply the 0-9999 board

numericProof.formula: factor = 1 + (lineupScarcity - reference) * sensitivity

findings.userImpact: A user selecting the adjusted board gets every trade value multiplied by a number derived from rest-of-season ordinal ranks. The direction is plausible and bounded (MAX_TOTAL_ADJUSTMENT 0.25, observed +-4.5%), but the quantity is not the cardinal scarcity the name implies, and the /rankings toggle says nothing about ROS being its input.

priorFinding.note: Priors reference rosValue scale mixing at the tag call sites (A01-F14 / A02-F06 / A19-F13) but none trace rosValue through compute_scarcity into the adjusted board that the engines serve.

findings.whatWorks: The coupling is dimensionally SAFE - a ratio of rosValues cancels units, so this is not the 0-9999-vs-0-100 error of W29-F005. Guardrails are real: evidence tier is STRUCTURAL_ONLY, absent axes contribute exactly 0, MAX_TOTAL_ADJUSTMENT clamps to +-25%, monotonicityViolations is empty on the live board, and docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md records that the adjusted board is deliberately a toggle rather than the default because four backtest framings found no improvement.
findings.rootCause: ROS is the only per-player quantity the platform has that is defined over a full roster including bench, so it is the only thing an endogenous lineup solve can run on. That is a real constraint, not an oversight.
findings.requiredRepair: Two separable steps. (1) Cheap and correct now: state the input in the overlay payload (a scarcityBasis: 'rosValue-ordinal' stamp) and in the /rankings toggle copy, so the lens does not read as board-derived. (2) The real fix: measure lineup scarcity from realized weekly scoring under the league's rate card - the same source scripts/measure_te_demand_actuals.py already uses - rather than from projection point estimates, which replacement.py itself shows understate flex demand for high-variance positions.
findings.dependencies: Step 2 depends on weekly actuals coverage; src/bdvm/actuals.py already scores nflverse weekly rows under exact league settings.

findings.title: trade-logic.js::displayValue ignores the user's per-player value override and its docstring describes a pick-year discount effectiveValue does not apply

findings.observed: effectiveValue (:181-185) applies no pick-year discount at all - it returns row.customValue when set, else row.values[valueMode]. The stated reason for displayValue's existence is therefore stale; the pick-year discount is applied in the backend pipeline (stage 12, config/weights/pick_year_discount.json) and is already baked into the value both functions read. The two functions now differ in exactly one way the docstring does not mention: displayValue (:203-209) never consults customValue, so a user's typed override drives the trade math but not any surface that renders through displayValue. findings.requiredRepair: Correct the docstring to state the real difference (customValue awareness), and make displayValue honour customValue so the two cannot diverge on a row inside a side. If a genuine 'show the board number, not the override' surface is wanted, name it that.

findings.title: Both playoff-odds engines publish 100%/0% certainty with zero games played and 14 weeks remaining, and the convergence check passes on it
findings.claimUnderTest: playoff_odds.py: 'Run N Monte Carlo simulations… sample each owner's score from their empirical distribution.' The v1 module documents collapse to 0/1 only for the season-over case ('remaining_weeks == 0').
findings.observed: Live payload: weeksPlayed=0, weeksRemaining=14, numSims=10000, scheduleCertainty='posted', every owner currentWins=0 and currentPointsFor=0.0 — and every playoffProbability is exactly 1.0 or exactly 0.0. v2 is the same shape at n_simulations=2000 and reports converged=true with worstPlayoffOddsSe=0.0: the standard error is zero because every simulation returns the identical answer, so the convergence gate certifies a degenerate result. rosChampionship inherits it — Roy shows playoffOdds 1.0, medianFinalSeed 3 and championshipOdds 0.0 simultaneously.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league/playoffOdds' | python -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin)['data'];print(d['weeksPlayed'],d['weeksRemaining'],d['numSims']);print(sorted({r['playoffProbability'] for r in d['owners']}))"
reproduction.expected: a spread of probabilities strictly between 0 and 1 with 14 weeks unplayed

numericProof.formula: count(distinct playoffProbability) over 12 owners

findings.userImpact: A manager opens /league in August and is told his team has a 0% chance of making the playoffs before a single snap. Trade-deadline direction (src/ros/direction.py) reads these same odds, so the same input drives a 'Strong Seller' recommendation.

priorFinding.note: reproduced live with exact payload values; the additional observation is that v2's convergence gate (converged=true, worstPlayoffOddsSe=0.0) certifies the degenerate output.

findings.whatWorks: scheduleCertainty is reported honestly ('posted'), and both engines publish weeksPlayed/weeksRemaining so a caller COULD suppress the section.
findings.rootCause: With no scored weeks, every owner's empirical distribution is the same league-wide fallback, so every simulation produces the same standings and the tie-break (PF, all zero) resolves deterministically.
findings.requiredRepair: Refuse to publish odds when weeksPlayed == 0 (the same posture the codebase uses for unpriced BDVM players), or seed preseason means from a projection source rather than an empty history.

findings.title: Three Python ports of KTC's Value Adjustment ship simultaneously and one of them rounds differently; its own parity test's ±1 tolerance is exactly the size of the divergence
findings.claimUnderTest: All three modules claim to be verbatim/line-for-line ports of frontend/lib/trade-logic.js::ktcAdjustPackage. trade_grading.py:103-112 states explicitly that Python's builtin round() is round-half-to-even and gives the wrong answer where JS gives another, and defines _js_round = floor(x+0.5) to avoid it.
findings.observed: src/trade/ktc_va.py — the port used by trade suggestions, the angle finder and the Monte Carlo sim — still calls Python's round() at :116 (ktc_reverse_adjust) and :319 (the returned value). The other two ports use floor(x+0.5). Over 20,000 random packages the ktc_va result differs from market_value_adjustment on 38 of them (0.19%), always by exactly 1; side and displayed never differ. ktc_va's own parity test asserts agreement 'to ±1', so the test cannot fail on this.

numericProof.formula: ktc_adjust_package(A,B).value

findings.userImpact: A package graded on /trade (JS) and the same package graded by trade suggestions can differ by one point of value adjustment. The magnitude is tiny; the fact that one algorithm has three maintained copies is not.

priorFinding.note: prior said 'three independent ports with no test tying two of them together'. Measured: the untied pair diverges on 0.19% of packages, always by 1, and the rounding function is the cause.

findings.whatWorks: Side selection and the display gate agree across all three ports on all 20,000 trials — the divergence is confined to the final rounding.
findings.rootCause: Three ports were written at different times; only two adopted the JS-rounding shim, and the third's parity test tolerance hides the gap.
findings.requiredRepair: Collapse to one port. If that is deferred, at minimum change ktc_va.py's two round() calls to floor(x+0.5) and tighten its parity tolerance to 0.
